Breaking: Review: Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres (Hyatt Inclusive)

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that of note, I was in Cancun, Mexico for business meetings at another resort but wanted to evaluate both this experience for our readers as well as the overall position of Hyatt in its ever-growing Inclusives collection.
  • Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres is an adults-only resort in the Hyatt Inclusive Collection, and I toured it on a site visit in November 2026.
  • Address: Carretera Punta Sam – Isla Blanca, Mz 2, Lt 10, Costa Mujeres, Zona Continental Isla Mujeres, Quintana Roo 77400, Mexico.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that of note, I was in Cancun, Mexico for business meetings at another resort but wanted to evaluate both this experience for our readers as well as the overall position of Hyatt in its ever-growing Inclusives collection. My stay was almost exactly 24 hours and solo which is uncharacteristic at this destination resort. My experience will likely differ from other guests due to those factors.

Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres is an adults-only resort in the Hyatt Inclusive Collection, and I toured it on a site visit in November 2026. It sits on a stretch of white-sand beach in Costa Mujeres, 12 miles north of Cancun. Cancun International Airport is the arrival airport. I could not confirm a single official transfer time from the property page. Tour listings commonly put the drive in a 30 to 45 minute range.

Address: Carretera Punta Sam – Isla Blanca, Mz 2, Lt 10, Costa Mujeres, Zona Continental Isla Mujeres, Quintana Roo 77400, Mexico.

Google Maps: Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres.

According to recent reports, hyatt is the best in the business at high end resort arrivals. I had given my name at the security gate and by the time I reached the lobby, the door to the vehicle was opened for me, I was greeted by name and a “welcome home”, a constant refrain throughout my stay. It’s a small thing and maybe cliché but it was effective. I was given a Globalist upgrade even though rules at all-inclusives differ from the rest of the chain. As my upgrade was in a Preferred room, I was brought into a private room at the front of the lobby where check-in was done for me.

The lobby is an open-air room under an arched woven ceiling, with a direct view out to the ocean.

Industry observers note that the resort is spread across 10 buildings with 505 keys. Of those, 221 are Preferred Club keys with an elevated experience. My building (and others like it) had just five rooms on each floor and just five floors which made it feel boutique rather than massive. Every oceanfront room is Preferred Club, and so are the first two buildings on either side.

In a recent development, the room views follow a simple rule by floor. Every first floor room is a swim-out, floors two through four are tropical view, and the fifth floor is ocean view or ocean front. That makes booking easy to reason through: if you want to step off your patio into the water, go low, and if you want the sea, go high.

Recent findings suggest that the walkways give a sense of grandeur and space. All of the flora is local, and in a touch I loved, the service rooms are named after the plants.

According to recent reports, there are four pools, and each one has a unique characteristic. The Jungle pool is drinks only and hidden in the middle of the resort by trees. The Social pool runs activities throughout the day at this adults-only resort for those who want to participate. There is also an infinity pool on the edge of the beach, and then the Preferred Club pool for those staying in that category. These are separate from the first floor swim-outs.

The spa (hydrotherapy is included for Preferred guests) featured an outdoor circuit that included both hot and cold plunge pools, amongst other therapeutic services.

The Preferred Club pool was the most frequented, though some images below look more vacant due to rain that rolled through during my opportunity to collect media on my short stay.

The gym is open to every guest from 6 AM to 8 PM, and it is outfitted with Technogym equipment.

According to recent reports, the spa is open 8 AM to 8 PM with 17 treatment cabins and a beauty salon, and hydrotherapy is included. That last part is the headline. The hydrotherapy space is ridiculous, easily the standout of the entire property for me, and it is the kind of amenity that would make me pick this resort over a competitor down the beach. There are indoor and outdoor showers as well.

The men’s changing room featured private showers with an option for indoor or outdoor experiences.

The theater seats 264 people and hosts cabaret and Mayan shows. There are also pickleball courts, which I am starting to think should be required equipment at any resort that wants a younger crowd as well as padel for the European set (and growing American interest.).

Secrets is an adults-only brand, and every room here comes with what the tech giant calls Unlimited-Luxury. For a standard guest that means unlimited dining and top-shelf drinks, Wi-Fi, daytime activities and nightly entertainment, with tips and taxes included. Add 24-hour room service, a mini-bar refreshed daily (you can ask for just about anything you want in there), and pool and beach wait service for all guests.

Recent findings suggest that the Preferred Club is an upgrade, and at this resort it is a significant one because it owns the oceanfront. Secrets lists personalized check-in and check-out, afternoon hot and cold hors d’oeuvres, desserts and premium liquors, access to the Preferred Club lounge and beach bar, an upgraded mini-bar, upgraded bath amenities, butler service, Bali beds at the pool and beach reserved for club guests, and exclusive dining at the Preferred Club beach restaurant. Preferred also gives club guests exclusive access to an infinity pool and puts an oversized soaking tub on the terrace of the upgraded suites (at least with the oceanfronts).

In a recent development, I book a lot of Hyatt’s all-inclusives through Hyatt Privé rates, and this resort is one of 388 in the collection. Privé is Hyatt’s invitation-only program for travel advisors, so you only get the benefits when an approved advisor makes the booking, and the stay still earns World of Hyatt points and elite nights.

It has been revealed that the all-inclusive version of Privé looks a lot different from a Park Hyatt booking. As I wrote when Hyatt’s all-inclusive resorts joined Privé, there is no room upgrade and no breakfast benefit, since every meal is already included. At this property, Privé guests receive a $100 resort credit per stay, a welcome amenity and letter, hydrotherapy access, and early check-in and late check-out based on availability.

Industry observers note that elite status matters here more than at most all-inclusives. Under World of Hyatt’s terms, Globalists get the best room available at check-in, including rooms with club access, at the resort’s discretion. Explorists are eligible for upgrades too, but not to standard suites or club rooms. Travelers who have stayed at Secrets resorts as Globalists report being designated Preferred Club guests even when they did not land in a club building, which unlocks the lounge, pool and beach areas. This was my experience on all accounts at the resort. Late checkout is 2 PM for Explorists and 4 PM for Globalists, subject to availability at resorts. It was able to honor my request for a late check-out, I did not arrive early enough to request the early check-in. Hyatt waives resort fees on eligible paid rates (at least for now) and award nights for Globalists, and on award nights only for every other tier, and Globalists also get free parking on free nights though in 2028 Globalists will have to select this as a preference. One catch is that Suite Upgrade Awards cannot be used at Secrets resorts, so you cannot lock in a suite with one here.

According to recent reports, weddings are substantial business here. The courtyard outside the theater is the setting, with the sunset behind it, and the resort hosts lots of them. The resort disclosed its occupancy to me but it wasn’t clear if it was for public consumption. It was shockingly high especially for a Thursday in mid-November. Over the holidays or spring break all the hotels are full but this is a period where I would have expected a lull. Still, despite being extremely full, it never felt crowded.

For meetings and groups, the convention space measures 9,800 square feet and splits into five sections. The boardroom was occupied at the time so I couldn’t include images of that.

In a recent development, restaurants can be booked in advance through the Hyatt Inclusive Collection app, which I wish more all-inclusives offered. Nobody wants to find out at 7 PM that the restaurant they wanted is full and through the app this can be done well in advance of a guest’s arrival. The dress code in the restaurants is resort casual, though the patio does not require slacks and closed toed shoes for men, shorts are acceptable outside.

The restaurants include: Portofino (Italian), Bordeaux (French), Himitsu (pan-Asian, with sushi and teppanyaki), Oceana (seafood in an open-air setting), Barefoot Grill (light lunch), Market Café (the international buffet, which I noted on site as the Marketplace), Seaside Grill (a poolside grill), and Coco Café. The bars on that list include Rendezvous in the lobby, Barracuda on the beach, a swim-up bar, a beach bar, and the Preferred Club beach bar and lounge bar. There’s also a Sports Bar and Lounge next to the theater.

Oceana is the seafood restaurant, set in an open-air dining room with woven pendant lamps, macrame hangings and a pebble mosaic floor. I chose this for my one dinner on property during my brief stay.

In a recent development, I started with the lamb croquettes, which the menu serves with yogurt and sweet chili sauce, cashews, watercress and a pickled shallot salad, and the Iberian salad with fresh mozzarella, prosciutto, rucula, toasted pistachios, balsamic and roasted peach. A crusty loaf came with the meal.

For a main I had the coconut shrimp, served with parsley orzo pasta, coconut sauce and parmesan crispy, and finished with the mango cheesecake, which the menu plates with vanilla cream and a mango compote with honey and basil.

In a recent development, market Café, the international buffet I noted as the Marketplace, serves breakfast until 11:30 AM. [TO CONFIRM: lunch and dinner service at Market Café].

Industry observers note that seaside Grill hosts the Preferred Club à la carte breakfast. The official dining page says breakfast there is served for Preferred Club guests only. I tried a number of dishes for lunch to report to our fine audience.

Rendezvous sits at the heart of the property with 360-degree access, so you can walk up to it from any direction.

Preferred Club guests get their own bar at the beach, and the Preferred Club lounge also has an indoor lounge for when the sun gets to be too much.

My room was a Preferred Oceanfront King, a single open room with a king bed against a macrame headboard wall, rattan pendant lights, a ceiling fan, and a daybed sofa facing a marble bistro table. The balcony with jacuzzi looks straight over the beach. In the bathroom, a freestanding tub sits under a wood-slat ceiling beside a walk-in rain shower with a pebble floor and a bench. The double vanity has vessel sinks, round mirrors and a wave-textured wall, and the shower is stocked with Le Labo Bergamote 22 shampoo, conditioner and shower gel. Le Labo is a confirmed winner for me.

I also had the chance to tour a master suites, all of which are oceanfront, and they are also available as swim-outs.

Every first floor room is a swim-out, opening onto the pool.

Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres is an incredible resort that somehow felt small when you were in your building but substantial enough to have everything. For my stay, I used 45,000 points on a no-notice booking to offset a $1,300/night stay. I have seen rates from $560 for off-season which is without question worth it. I loved the property and I look forward to returning with more time and my wife, but the adults-only nature of the property will make it a harder stay for us to achieve.

What do you think? Have you stayed at Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres?

The 10 Best Places to Retire in the US

📅 29 Jun 2022 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that it’s all about living life your way and celebrating your passions.
  • According to recent reports, to help guide that decision, WalletHub has released its annual Best & Worst Places to Retire list—a ranking of 182 cities across the US (including the 150 most populated US cities, plus at least two of the most populated cities in each state) based on affordability, activities, quality of life, and healthcare.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, these days, retirement can come in many different forms—and arrive at many different ages. Some may choose to spend their golden years indulging in new hobbies, sports, and skills, while others may decide to focus on spending more quality time with family or take off and travel the world.

Recent findings suggest that it’s all about living life your way and celebrating your passions. But no matter when you choose to pull the career plug, everyone deserves to find a home base that can best support your newfound lifestyle. After all, not being tied down to an office or career means you can finally move to your dream city, or bop between your favorite travel destinations.

According to recent reports, to help guide that decision, WalletHub has released its annual Best & Worst Places to Retire list—a ranking of 182 cities across the US (including the 150 most populated US cities, plus at least two of the most populated cities in each state) based on affordability, activities, quality of life, and healthcare. Unsurprisingly, four Florida cities made the Top 10—including claiming all top three spots—powered by the state's tax-free policies and warm weather.

Here are the 10 best places to retire in the US, according to this year’s WalletHub study, along with supporting data we’ve pulled from the US Census Bureau, Zillow, city governments, and the demographic data firm Best Places. Whether you end up chasing sunshine or snowflakes, small towns or urban hubs, the words “retirement home” could be much more exciting than you think.

This gallery has been updated with fresh information since its original publication date.

According to recent reports, with dramatic rivers and bridges dotting its scenery, and a culture and food scene that is constantly reinventing itself, Pittsburgh isn’t just a place to be—it’s a place to make home. Even with all the benefits of an urban hub, housing prices are generally lower than in most of the country. Pittsburgh is also known for having some of the best hospitals in the nation, with an array of social services designed to take care of senior residents. The list of activities to do here is endless, whether it’s taking the Duquesne or Monongahela inclines to see sky-high views of the river confluences, or exploring the latest exhibits at local museums like the Carnegie Museum of Art and Andy Warhol Museum, or the quirky Randyland. And of course, the food options here are diverse and delightful, from Italian neighborhood favorite DiAnoia’s Eatery to take-out from Lucy’s Banh Mi, lovingly made and served out of a makeshift trailer.

Population: 302,971 (median age: 34.4 years).

Industry observers note that cost of living: The median home price is $234,620, over $130,000 less than the national median. Rent is also significantly lower, with the average being $1,550.

Industry observers note that income tax on social security? No.

Climate: 160 sunny days per year; average lows of 21°F in winter; average highs of 84°F in summer.

Healthcare: Pittsburgh has 38.1 physicians per 10,000 residents, above the US average.

According to recent reports, honestly, could there be a better place to retire? Charleston is the best of every world, starting with a burgeoning culinary scene. Among the standouts are southern staples like Miller’s All Day and Callie’s Hot Little Biscuit, seafood spots like Leon’s Oyster Shop and Hank’s Seafood Restaurant, and modern favorites Chubby Fish, Frannie and the Fox, and Bar 167. Add to that a walkable downtown (including the local open-air market hall Charleston City Market) and waterfront (with the iconic Pineapple Fountain!).

Population: 150,227 (median age: 36.6 years).

In a recent development, cost of living: The median home cost in Charleston is $587,511—about 1.6 the national median. The average rent is $3,000 (an increase of about $100 since last year).

In a recent development, income tax on social security? No.

Climate: 209 sunny days per year; average lows of 39°F in winter; average highs of 90°F in summer.

Healthcare: Charleston has 47.8 physicians per 10,000 residents (above the national average).

In a recent development, while Fort Lauderdale may be best known for its beaches, the city’s appeal extends far beyond the coastline these days. With a plethora of waterfront condos to call home, days can be spent touring art galleries in Flagler Village, taking cooking classes at Sistrunk Market, or birding at Hugh Taylor Birch State Park and Secret Woods Nature Center. Plus, sports fans will love the roster of teams to cheer on, like soccer and hockey—and Miami Heat and Miami Dolphins’ home stadiums are both a short drive away.

Population: 182,760 (median age: 42.5 years).

In a recent development, cost of living: The median home cost in Fort Lauderdale is $509,743—a slight drop from last year, but still much higher than the national median. The average rent is $2,700 (an increase of about $100 since last year).

Income tax on social security? No.

Climate: 246 sunny days per year; average lows of 59°F in winter; average highs of 90°F in summer.

Healthcare: Fort Lauderdale has 22.4 physicians per 10,000 residents (above the national average).

It has been revealed that as long as you can tolerate some mightily cold winters, retiring in Minneapolis means you’re never far from great independent retailers, worthwhile museums, scenic lakes, and dining experiences that extend far beyond the tater tot hotdish. Despite falling four rankings from last year, the City of Lakes still has plenty going for it. The best part? “Minnesota nice” is a very real thing, so there’s a pretty good chance you’ll end up with a friendly neighbor.

Population: 429,954 (median age: 33.3 years).

Industry observers note that cost of living: The median home cost in Minneapolis is $328,351, which is lower than the national median. The average rent is a reasonable $1,717.

Income tax on social security? Yes.

Climate: 198 sunny days per year; average lows of 7°F in winter; average highs of 84°F in summer.

Healthcare: Minneapolis has 33.9 physicians per 10,000 residents (above the national average).

Industry observers note that atlanta is chock full of activities, be it museums, sports, live music, or just getting outside and taking it all in. All that and more contributes to the Georgia capital ranking 4 out of 170 in Wallethub’s activities index. One newly introduced attraction is the Atlanta Beltline, a greenway that's currently being built around the city, which debuted its Southside and Southeast trails this year. Travel lovers will also appreciate being near Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport—the busiest international airport in the world. And don’t forget to mix in the city’s innovative Southern food scene, with diverse highlights like Mary Mac’s Tea Room, Rina, and Botiwalla by Chai Pani.

Population: 498,715 (median age: 34.5 years).

Industry observers note that cost of living: The median home cost in Atlanta is $380,331, which is higher than the national median. The average rent is $2,089, above the national average.

Income tax on social security? No.

Climate: 217 sunny days per year; average lows of 33°F in winter; average highs of 88°F in summer.

Healthcare: Atlanta has 36.5 physicians per 10,000 residents (above the national average).

It has been revealed that if city life isn’t quite how you imagined spending your golden years, Casper, Wyoming, is perfect for those seeking a Ron Swanson-style retirement. Spend your days fly-fishing, canoeing, and hiking right outside your door—not to mention day-trip access to Grand Teton and Rocky Mountain national parks. In terms of culture, there are plenty of art museums, planetariums, and historic sites to continue that sense of exploration. As an added bonus, it’s by far one of the least expensive towns on this list—WalletHub ranked it 3rd out of 182 for affordability. It’s no wonder it leaped five spots from last year up to fifth place.

Population: 59,038 (median age: 37.3 years).

Cost of living: The median home sale price in Casper is $310,650, which is lower than the national median. The average rent is $1,350, up $150 from last year.

In a recent development, income tax on social security? No.

Climate: 220 sunny days per year; average lows of 15°F in winter; average highs of 88°F in summer.

Healthcare: Casper has 19.7 physicians per 10,000 residents (a bit below the national average).

As the No. 1 city in WalletHub's quality of life metric, Scottsdale is easily one of the best places to retire in the US, despite sinking two spots from last year. It is a famously popular spot for golfers, but it also boasts plenty of destination spas, incredible art and architecture, and James Beard Award-winning restaurants to satisfy retirees of all types. Another upside: 330 sunny days a year. Just be prepared for really, really hot summers—average temperatures from June to September are all in the triple digits.

Population: 241,361 (median age: 53 years).

Cost of living: The median home cost in Scottsdale is $851,746, which is nearly 2.3 times higher than the national median. The median rent is $3,400 per month, more than $1,400 above the national median.

It has been revealed that income tax on social security? No.

Climate: 330 sunny days per year; average lows of 42°F in winter; average highs of 104°F in summer.

Healthcare: Scottsdale has 20.1 physicians per 10,000 residents (below the national average).

In a recent development, tampa, on Florida's Gulf Coast, rose two spots to capture the bronze medal this year. The city itself has plenty of housing options, a buzzing Riverwalk, and one of the best airports in the country. With plenty of surrounding suburbs, it also makes a great jumping-off point for exploring other beach towns in the state. Foodies should take note, as Tampa is known for its restaurants—Rooster & the Till (run by James Beard semi-finalist Ferrell Alvarez) and 384,959 (median age: 36.3 years) (beloved for its Cuban sandwiches) are two stand-outs.

Population: 384,959 (median age: 36.3 years).

Cost of living: The median home cost in Tampa is $375,619, up just 0.4 percent over last year. The average rent is $1,962/month, down $95 since last year.

Income tax on social security? No.

Climate: 246 sunny days per year; average lows of 52°F in winter; average highs of 90°F in summer.

Healthcare: Tampa has 24.3 physicians per 10,000 residents (above the national average).

Miami rose two spots since last year to the runner-up position. It may not be quite as affordable as other cities, but Miami has enough art galleries, Cuban food, golf courses, beaches, and museums to justify the rent. (And who wouldn’t love the chance to drive down to Key West whenever they want?) Miami-Dade County even offers an “Active Older Adults Program” that provides free fitness classes, games, field trips and arts activities for people ages 55 and older. Plus it ranks the sixth most walkable city on this list, with most residents having access to public transportation within walking distance of their homes.

Population: 442,241 (median age: 41.2 years).

According to recent reports, cost of living: The median home cost in Miami is $583,705, which is up 1.4% from last year. The average rent is $3,100, the same as last year.

Income tax on social security? No.

Climate: 248 sunny days per year; average lows of 61°F in winter; average highs of 89°F in summer.

Healthcare: Miami has 22.8 physicians per 10,000 residents (above the national average).

It has been revealed that for the third year in a row, Orlando snagged the trophy for the most retiree-friendly city in the nation. We’ve already mentioned the warm weather and low taxes of Florida, but Orlando has a particular abundance of quiet communities, great restaurants, and independent stores—and its inland location means you won’t have to worry quite as much during hurricane season. (Bonus: Given Orlando’s proximity to theme parks, it’ll be easy to convince family to visit, too.).

Population: 307,573 (median age: 35.4 years).

According to recent reports, income tax on social security? No.

Climate: 233 sunny days per year; average lows of 49°F in winter; average highs of 92°F in summer.

  • Last June, JetBlue debuted a status match that put elites from competing carriers into Mosaic 1 or Mosaic 2.
  • Industry observers note that my application was approved just before the June 30 deadline.
  • My two primary airports are Pittsburgh, PA (PIT) and Fort Myers, FL (RSW).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last June, JetBlue debuted a status match that put elites from competing carriers into Mosaic 1 or Mosaic 2. It also offered a faster track for Delta Diamond, Delta 360, AA Executive Platinum and Concierge Key members: earn 50 tiles by year-end and get Mosaic 4. That worked out to $5,000 in JetBlue flights or Paisly packages, or $50,000 on the JetBlue card, and a single Mint roundtrip to Europe could cover most of it. I already had AA Executive Platinum, so I didn’t need the status. I wanted it anyway. JetBlue was adding routes from my home airports, I fly to Boston, New York and Fort Lauderdale often, and the United partnership raised the possibility of benefits on both sides.

Industry observers note that my application was approved just before the June 30 deadline. Some applicants waited up to six weeks for processing, though, and losing six weeks of a 12-week challenge is a real cost. JetBlue then added its 25-for-25 promotion on top. Visiting 25 destinations by year-end earned up to 350,000 TrueBlue points plus 25 years of Mosaic 1, which made a cheap, aggressive weekend of short hops look worth it. My plan was to finish the challenge through spend and put the points toward transatlantic and Japan trips. My one worry at the time was whether JetBlue would treat these newly introduced Mosaics well enough to keep them flying with it.

My two primary airports are Pittsburgh, PA (PIT) and Fort Myers, FL (RSW). I occasionally also fly from Fort Lauderdale or Miami when it makes sense. But Pittsburgh had just flights to Boston for some of last year, before adding Fort Lauderdale to fill the Spirit gap and then Fresh York JFK competing with Delta, and more broadly to the New York market, United and American with more than enough flights. From Fort Myers, it’s Boston of JFK.

Recent findings suggest that I flew once to Boston on JetBlue but at the time, it had not yet introduced a domestic first class, a better seat selection included in my fare was the only real enhancement to the short flight of just over 80 minutes. I’ll cover other reasons why I wasn’t able to fly the carrier more, but given that I am not in Upcoming York, Boston, or Fort Lauderdale full time, every flight I take has a connection and it’s not particularly on-the-way for me. For example, if heading south to Florida, Charlotte, Atlanta, or even Washington Dulles make more sense than Boston or New York but when heading west at all, Chicago, Houston, Dallas, and Denver are all obviously better options.

Even to Europe, there’s not a material advantage with limited schedules and limited footprint on the continent. For trips to Paris given that I will have to connect anyway, I have more options on any other carrier through east coast hubs than with JetBlue on its metal not to mention partner networks.

Most recently, I had a flight to Cancun and with airport time, flight time and connections, it’s faster to fly out of Miami or Fort Lauderdale. But JetBlue had fewer flights for more money and far more miles than with American. Outside of the northeast corridor or based in South(east) Florida, I couldn’t make it make sense.

I’m heading to Europe for a meeting next week and I will finally have a chance to try Mint. This will constitute two of my longest flights with JetBlue ever. I haven’t heard many negative comments about JetBlue Mint, and I have high expectations. It’s hard to get excited about another American or United flight in business class solely because I have flown those so often and there’s little newly introduced there.

I’ll get a chance to try a reasonably long three-hour flight domestically to see how it differs from my prior JetBlue experience. Then, assuming flights are on time, I should have a chance to try the new BlueHouse, a first for me. Following that is a long haul flight in Mint and I am looking forward to the experience.

It has been revealed that statistically, I can’t see a reason that I try for Mosaic again, but who knows? The experience could change what appears to be a clear analytical decision for me at this point.

One of the biggest reasons I secure status via flying/spending/staying is to redeem systemwide upgrades (or suite upgrades in the case of hotels.) I’ll fully admit that upon receiving approval for the challenge last year, I hadn’t even considered that Mint certificates would work differently than other upgrade certificates in the industry. One upgrade certificate is worth an upgrade (if available.) United uses “Plus Points” but it feels clearer that there will be some variability in what’s required to move between the cabins.

For this particular trip, JetBlue wanted two upgrade certificates in one direction, and four on another. Thankfully, I had taken the upgrade option every time I achieved a choice to select a benefit, but had I chosen something else assuming that I’d only need two Move to Mint certificates (as I would with American for example) I would have come up short.

I covered how much spending is required to achieve top tier status and its associated benefits in recent posts. This was in response to United’s move to require $480,000 in annual spending (by credit card only) to achieve United 1K status. Assuming that along the way loyalty points are taken and annual Mosaic bonuses are applied to cardholders, JetBlue is above American at $225,000 in spend for Mosaic 4 vs. American’s net of $164,000 for Executive Platinum with just two systemwide upgrades, or $214,000 with six. The difference is that those six upgrades apply for the full-one-way on a single certificate.

I spent time trying to figure out why one way charged four Move to Mint vs two and in the end, it didn’t really matter. I can nearly upgrade my entire family of four on American vs a single roundtrip for myself. For what it’s worth, the base cost was also more expensive with JetBlue than American for which I had upgrades available.

Industry observers note that I have the qualified business spend to earn Mosaic 4 every year, but the value of its perks aren’t even close to the rest of the market. And for what JetBlue expects in spend compared to what I could earn elsewhere is uncompetitive.

And as a side note, the fixed rate of JetBlue points (about 1.4¢/each) is unimpressive but for most of the attempts I tried to use them throughout the year both domestically and internationally, they proved of little value. A lack of partners is much the same. I looked at a redemption in Mint on my flights to Europe and though I had more than 220,000, it was an insufficient balance for the simple roundtrip. For context, I took United a few years ago on miles and redeemed 160,000 roundtrip (this year was available at 176,000 roundtrip) and multiple times in the last 24 months on American at or around 115,000 roundtrip. Miles aren’t worth enough, they aren’t flexible enough, and there aren’t enough partners to fill gaps in the JetBlue map.

It has been revealed that I had higher expectations for JetBlue based on the experiences of my peers. I think its equipment is excellent, but widespread first class availability is a necessity. The limited utility of Move to Mint certificates were the nail in the coffin and the usability of the miles didn’t help. But even then, I really want to love and fly JetBlue, and I am willing to go a little out of my way to use them. But I’m not willing to fly backwards for fewer flights at a higher cost.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

JetBlue is growing its presence in Central America and the Caribbean.

Industry observers note that for the first time ever, the carrier will serve the Honduran capital of Tegucigalpa. Starting Feb. 25, 2027, flights from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, will arrive at Palmerola International Airport in Comayagua, which serves Tegucigalpa.

Right now, JetBlue’s only destination in Honduras is San Pedro Sula, in the country’s northwest.

In a recent development, on Feb. 23, the carrier will launch service between Fort Lauderdale and George Town, Grand Cayman, in the Cayman Islands.

Both routes will operate daily, using a mix of Airbus A320 and A220 aircraft.

Industry observers note that jetBlue will also offer limited-time daily service from Fort Lauderdale to Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, between Jan. 29 and Feb. 15. The connection will help travelers reach the islands during Carnival, the airline noted.

“We’re grateful for the way customers across South Florida continue to embrace JetBlue, and we’re committed to delivering even more of the destinations and travel options they’re looking for,” Daniel Shurz, JetBlue’s senior vice president of revenue, network, and enterprise planning, noted in a news release. “With new international service to Honduras and Grand Cayman, we’re strengthening Fort Lauderdale’s role as a key gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean, making it easier for customers to reconnect with loved ones, explore new places, and travel across our growing network.”.

In a recent development, american has prioritized Latin America as demand from U.S. markets, especially Miami, grows. The carrier just recently launched service to Barranquilla and Cali in Colombia and will add Barcelona, Venezuela, to its network in January.

    Traveling This Thanksgiving? Here’s the Latest on Flight Delays Following Delta Outage

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1444 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • On Sunday, November 22, US travelers faced another wave of significant flight disruptions ahead of Thanksgiving.
    • This time around, the challenges occurred at the nation’s busiest hub, Atlanta’s Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport (ATL), where Delta Air Lines delayed hundreds of flights due to a problem with a critical piece of technology.
    • Sources indicate that the delays sent ripple effects throughout the carrier's US network, snarling travel plans for thousands of Delta fliers heading out on Thanksgiving trips.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On Sunday, November 22, US travelers faced another wave of significant flight disruptions ahead of Thanksgiving.

    This time around, the challenges occurred at the nation’s busiest hub, Atlanta’s Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport (ATL), where Delta Air Lines delayed hundreds of flights due to a problem with a critical piece of technology.

    Sources indicate that the delays sent ripple effects throughout the carrier's US network, snarling travel plans for thousands of Delta fliers heading out on Thanksgiving trips. While the issue was resolved Sunday afternoon, the airline delayed 300 flights and canceled 92 flights on Monday morning, according to FlightAware. “Operations are stable today with automation for departing flight weight and balance calculations fully restored,” a Delta spokesperson told Traveler on Monday. “Delta teams are focused on keeping the operation moving safely and caring for our customers.”.

    In a recent development, for US travelers, the timing is particularly stressful. AAA projects 5.96 million travelers will take domestic flights over the Thanksgiving holiday period. Plus, Delta’s operational difficulties came only nine days after the FAA declared a rare nationwide ground stop on November 13 that lasted more than four hours and led to multiple days of travel chaos.

    It has been revealed that while Delta’s technology challenges had nothing to do with the FAA systems, both incidents have travelers questioning if their Thanksgiving travel aims will be disrupted. Here’s a look at the current situation and what travelers should know before heading to the airport this week.

    This article has been updated with fresh information since its original publish date.

    On Sunday morning, Delta began having issues with its weight and balance automation system at the Atlanta airport. The system’s critical equipment assesses whether aircraft are too heavy to fly before takeoff.

    While the system was out, Delta crews use manual backup processes to help flights depart. However, the technology outage still led to thousands of delays and hundreds of cancellations.

    Delta had 2,194 flight delays on November 22, which is about 64% of its schedule, according to FlightAware data. The carrier also had 274 canceled flights on Sunday. Although some of those disruptions were due to other issues, like bad weather in the Northeast, Delta noted that 70% of the flight changes were caused by the ATL equipment problems, according to CNN.

    It has been revealed that the airline said it had restored the system by Sunday afternoon. By Monday morning, Delta’s flight schedules across the country appeared to be getting back on track. However, as of 11 a.m. ET on Monday, the carrier had accumulated more than 300 flight delays and 92 cancellations, FlightAware showed. Now that the technology issue has been resolved, travelers can expect Delta's flight schedule to progressively return to normal but should still prepare for lingering delays through Tuesday, November 24.

    Recent findings suggest that travelers with canceled flights can ask for a full cash refund if they no longer wish to travel. The carrier doesn’t charge passengers to change their flights if they’re booked in any fare class except basic economy (although a difference in fare may apply).

    According to recent reports, passengers should continue to check with Delta for the latest information on their flight status. When traveling for Thanksgiving, err on the side of caution and initiative to arrive at the airport early: at least two hours before a domestic flight and three hours before an international one.

    Recent findings suggest that the ground stop on November 13 was due to a separate matter with air traffic control equipment outages and the telecommunications systems that the FAA uses to track and communicate with planes while they’re flying. “The ground stop was issued out of an abundance of caution,” states the FAA’s statement. “Safety is, and will always remain, the FAA’s highest priority. We will never compromise the safety of the flying public.”.

    Recent findings suggest that on November 13, the FAA’s network service provider, L3Harris, was updating telecommunications equipment at an FAA facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, when the issues began, according to the FAA. The firm was deploying a new router that also began to cause system disruptions at a radar site in Amarillo, Texas. “The FAA’s legacy equipment became unstable when data began flooding the FAA FTI network, at a rate of 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds,” claims an FAA statement. “This disrupted the system and created instability with aircraft communications and radar feeds.”.

    Industry observers note that once the inconsistencies were identified, the FAA indicates that L3Harris blocked those two locations, and the network stabilized. However, the exact cause of the telecommunications issues are still under investigation.

    Recent findings suggest that regulators are still working to identify the root cause of the issue. “The work that was done on Friday, that's been done thousands of times by L3Harris in our network,” Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy mentioned in a recent interview on ABC’s “This Week.” “It's been done thousands of times by other companies, and these complications haven't arisen, and so that's why we have to figure out what went wrong here.”.

    Duffy also noted that the equipment in question is several decades old: the router was originally purchased in 2001 and was also part of a system that ran on obsolete copper wiring.

    Experts say that the archaic equipment underscores the urgent need to patch the nation’s air traffic control system. “While the investigation continues, the incident exposed a troubling reality: America's aviation system remains vulnerable because we have relied on aging infrastructure for far too long,” says Geoff Freeman, president and CEO of US Travel Association. The “disruption was a wake-up call that Washington cannot afford to ignore.”.

    For many US airlines, the busy Thanksgiving travel season began with early departures on November 19 and is expected to last through December 1.

    Air travel experts say that the FAA ground stop’s effects on Thanksgiving travel intends should be minimal. As of November 16, the majority of airline flight schedules were back on track. Delta was also able to restore its systems on Sunday, November 22; as of Monday, flight schedules began returning to normal but Delta fliers could still encounter lingering delays early this week.

    It helps that fewer travelers are expected to fly this Thanksgiving compared to recent years. According to Mike Arnot, spokesman for Cirium, an aviation analytics organization, the Wednesday before Thanksgiving is usually one of the busiest air travel days of the year. But in 2026, it’s not even slated to be in the top 50 busiest days for flying.

    Travelers should still continue to check with their airline for the latest travel updates and strategy to be at the airport at least two hours before takeoff for a domestic flight.

    Operations are largely back on track, so many airlines have ended the flexible rebooking waivers that were issued at the beginning of the ground stop.

    In a recent development, however, Delta is still allowing passengers who were scheduled to fly through Monday, November 16 to make changes to their flights at no extra cost through November 23. Customers' upcoming departure dates must be on or before November 23, according to the airline’s rebooking policy.

    Even if your airline no longer has a travel waiver in place, if you’re flying with a major US carrier, you likely have the ability to change your flight without paying a fee (although a difference in fare may apply). However, these policies usually do not apply to low-cost carriers or tickets booked in basic economy class.

    Sources indicate that it’s impossible to predict if a nationwide ground stop could happen again, according to Freeman of the US Travel Association. However, modernizing the air traffic control system should reduce these types of outages in the long run.

    “The FAA is making progress, replacing outdated copper communications lines with high-speed fiber, upgrading radar and radio systems, and introducing technology that allows air traffic controllers to manage flights more efficiently,” Freeman indicates. “For travelers, these investments should mean fewer delays, more reliable flights, and greater confidence that the system can handle disruptions.”.

    Recent findings suggest that airline executives echoed a similar sentiment regarding the state of US air traffic control systems. “This moment must be a call to action,” United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby said in a statement emailed to media. “It is critical for safety, our passengers, and our economy that we fix our nation’s Air Traffic Control system now.”.

    Following the ground stop, the DOT requested an additional $50.1 billion from Congress to complete its overhaul of the national air traffic control system.

    For more information on passenger rights during airline technology outages, read our full guide.

    Mary Peltola unseats Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (783 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that former Alaska Rep.
    • Mary Peltola has defeated Republican Sen.
    • According to recent reports, the Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that former Alaska Rep. Mary Peltola speaks during her election night party in Anchorage on Nov. 3. (Charly Triballeau/ AFP via Getty Images).

    Former Rep. Mary Peltola has defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, giving Senate Democrats their ninth pickup of the midterm elections and bringing their caucus’s total seats in the next Congress to 56.

    According to recent reports, the Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, a full two weeks after Election Day. The latest tranche of ballots counted put the former congresswoman past the 50-percent threshold to win the election outright without Alaska’s ranked choice voting system kicking in.

    With her victory, Peltola, who is Yup’ik, becomes one of the first Native American women elected to the Senate, along with fellow Democrat Peggy Flanagan, who won the open seat in Minnesota this month.

    “As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first.,” Peltola said in a statement after the race was called.

    The Alaska race was the final Senate contest to be called in a midterm election that saw Democrats win commanding majorities in both chambers of Congress. Besides Alaska, Democrats also flipped Senate seats in North Carolina, Maine, Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi.

    In a recent development, peltola, a former state legislator, made history in 2022 when she became the first Alaska Native elected to Congress, winning a special election for the state’s at-large district. She comfortably won the general election that fall but was narrowly unseated in 2024 by Republican Nick Begich.

    According to recent reports, she entered the Senate contest in January, positioning herself as an independent-minded Democrat and invoking the legacies of two well-liked Alaska Republicans, the late Sen. Ted Stevens and the late Rep. Don Young, whom she succeeded in the House.

    She campaigned on the slogan “fish, family, freedom” and played up her moderate views and deep roots in the state.

    Industry observers note that but the race was marked by allegations of political gamesmanship. In addition to the incumbent Sullivan, a retired colonel in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserves, the Senate ballot also included a retired teacher named Dan J. Sullivan. The New York Times reported late last month that operatives aligned with Peltola’s campaign were involved in the effort to recruit the second Dan Sullivan in an attempt to confuse voters.

    Peltola has said she had no connection to the scheme.

    Prior to Election Day, the Trump administration filed a lawsuit seeking to delay certification of the result if Sen. Sullivan were to lose. The lawsuit was tossed earlier this month by a federal judge.

    Trump also suggested that all votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan should be added to the incumbent’s total. “If you add them up, Dan Sullivan wins,” the president told reporters Monday. But as of Tuesday evening when the race was called, Peltola had more votes than both Sullivans combined.

    Recent findings suggest that the Alaska race was initially viewed as a long shot for Democrats. The Last Frontier has elected a Democratic senator just once in the past 50 years – in 2008, when Mark Begich ousted Stevens. Begich, the Democratic uncle of the current Republican congressman, served a single term before he was ousted by Sullivan in 2014.

    But anger in Alaska over the rising cost of food and fuel — already among the highest in the nation — provided Democrats with an opening.

    Recent findings suggest that "56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago," Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer said in a statement Tuesday night. "But I knew if we concentrated on getting the best candidates, and if we focused like a laser on the costs, corruption, and chaos that Donald Trump has wrought throughout America, we would have shot.".

    Recent findings suggest that in other Alaska races, Democrats flipped the governor’s mansion, with former state Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins winning an open-seat race to become the first Democrat elected governor of the state since Tony Knowles won a second term in 1998.

    Industry observers note that the race for the state’s at-large House district will be decided by ranked choice voting, with tabulations expected to take place Wednesday. Begich, the GOP incumbent, was leading Tuesday with 47.5 percent of the vote and is expected to prevail over independent Bill Hill, who had the backing of national Democrats and trailed with 42 percent. Another Democrat and a Libertarian combined for the remainder of the vote.

    Toxic Lufthansa Aims 1,000 Job Cuts But Cannot Explain Which Jobs Will Go

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (793 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Lufthansa prepares to eliminate 1,000 full-time positions at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs as management warns that its turnaround is falling short.
    • According to an internal letter to employees, Lufthansa management plans to cut approximately 1,000 full-time positions across its two main hubs.
    • The letter, signed by Lufthansa Airlines CEO Jens Ritter and his fellow board members, describes an airline struggling to become competitive.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Lufthansa prepares to eliminate 1,000 full-time positions at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs as management warns that its turnaround is falling short. The financial problems are real, but I am skeptical that another vaguely defined job-cut announcement will help an airline that desperately needs to make peace with its employees in order to ultimately succeed.

    According to an internal letter to employees, Lufthansa management plans to cut approximately 1,000 full-time positions across its two main hubs.

    The letter, signed by Lufthansa Airlines CEO Jens Ritter and his fellow board members, describes an airline struggling to become competitive. Management reported an adjusted operating loss of €180 million for the first nine months of 2026, an average of €20 million per month. It cited high fuel costs, the Middle East conflict, and nine strike days among the pressures on the business. Management also acknowledged shortcomings in costs, efficiency, and productivity.

    But several basic details remain unclear:.

    (That last point is particularly important).

    The pilot union Vereinigung Cockpit responded sharply, accusing management of using an ominous but imprecise announcement to pressure employees as labor negotiations remain unresolved. The union wants answers about which jobs are affected and whether these are additional reductions. It also argues that management must take responsibility for its own operational and strategic decisions.

    Ground-staff union Verdi has raised similar concerns. Proposed savings include consolidating technical and administrative work right now performed separately within the organization. There may be a sensible case for that, but telling employees that 1,000 positions will disappear without explaining where or how is an excellent way to spread anxiety far beyond the people ultimately affected….

    I keep thinking about my Lufthansa A340-600 flight from Frankfurt to Washington earlier this year.

    It was a superb flight, despite a business class seat that was well behind the competition. The improved food and bedding helped, but one of the main reasons I enjoyed it so much was the crew.

    Recent findings suggest that the flight attendants were friendly and engaging: the flight attendant working my side was so pleasant. I also sensed pride in delivering the improved onboard service, even though the upcoming service flow created more work.

    Those employees gave me a reason to look forward to flying Lufthansa again.

    It has been revealed that that anecdote certainly does not establish how many employees Lufthansa needs or whether its current labor agreements are sustainable (and this announcement does not suggest any crew positions are being cut). But my experience illustrates something management should remember as it tries to rebuild the business: good employees can make passengers want to come back, even when the seat itself is nothing special. And “happy employees make happy customers” include ground staff, lounge staff, and customer service folks too.

    Lufthansa has published its latest proposal to the pilot union, offering the prospect of up to 1,000 cockpit hires by 2033 and up to 150 additional captain promotions annually. In exchange, it seeks changes to compensation and productivity. The proposal also includes one-time payments for 2027 and 2028, with salary increases beginning in 2029.

    In a recent development, those prospective hires are a separate issue from the proposed hub job cuts. The different figures concern different roles and timeframes.

    In a recent development, management should not have to accept every union demand and employees also have an interest in a financially viable airline: reaching an agreement will require concessions. But Lufthansa must find a way to make peace with its workforce. The latest announcement has already inflamed matters, and I struggle to see how leaving so much uncertainty helps either side reach an agreement.

    Industry observers note that if Lufthansa can eliminate unnecessary duplication while protecting the operation and treating affected employees fairly, it should be clear about it. I want Lufthansa to succeed. My A340 flight reminded me how good it can be. I would hate to see the enthusiasm I encountered onboard become another casualty of the never-ending conflict between management and labor.

    Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 full-time positions in Frankfurt and Munich, but has yet to publicly explain several essential details, including whether those reductions are part of an existing program.

    Cost control is necessary, especially as market uncertainty and high oil prices continue. But so is a workforce willing to help deliver the airline that Lufthansa wants passengers to pay a premium to fly. My recent experience demonstrated how much its employees contribute, and I hope management can find a path to profitability that gives those employees a reason to remain invested in its success. Lufthansa is in desperate need of strong leadership…I’ll just leave it at that.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A cheese tray is hardly the most exciting thing you can order on an airplane, but American Airlines does this one very well. I recently enjoyed its buy-on-board fruit and cheese plate in economy class and would choose it over the comparable offerings on Delta or United. Let’s take a closer look in this week’s Meal of the Week.

    Industry observers note that american sells its fruit and cheese plate for $13 or 1,300 AAdvantage miles (please folks, don’t use miles to pay for it). The current selection includes:.

    I loved all three varieties of cheese (I’m not fan of bleu or brie, so very happy not to have to waste anything).

    The crackers were excellent too. That might sound like a minor detail, but good cheese deserves good crackers, and these complemented the cheese very well…oh how I loathe soda crackers.

    The apples were sweet and crisp, I enjoyed the single fig, and I loved finishing with the Toblerone. A little chocolate at the end was just right…that’s often my dessert at home too.

    I have enjoyed cheese plates on Delta and United too, but American offers the superior economy class version, in my opinion. I really liked the blueberry artigiano and smoked black pepper cheddar.

    This was a late evening flight where I had planned to eat in the lounge before my flight but due to a flight delay jumped onto an earlier flight. It was 8:00 pm, I had not eaten, and had I been flying on United I would have been out of luck since you have to pre-order any food onboard beyond snack boxes.

    I figured I would have to make a Taco Bell run in LA when I landed, but this proved enough..and my body thanks me.

    It has been revealed that american Airlines has a very good buy-on-board cheese plate. I enjoyed all three cheeses, the crackers were excellent, the apples were sweet, and the Toblerone was a nice dessert.

    In a recent development, simple food can be very satisfying when the ingredients are good. This is something American does better than Delta or United in economy class, and I would gladly order it again.

    p.s. If you’re still feeling peckish, you might also enjoy a bag of salted, mixed nuts from Nuts & Clark…$11 or 1,100 miles. Also recommended!

    Industry observers note that while I love staying at a really great five-star hotel, there is a time and place for renting an Airbnb. For me, it's when I'm vacationing in the Caribbean. On my most recent trip to the area, I holed up in a sprawling Puerto Rico villa with a path to the beach and a private pool overlooking the sea. My family and I spent most of our time barefoot, and there was room for everyone to spread out before gathering in the kitchen to whip up dinner. It’s one of my favorite memories—and one anyone can replicate almost anywhere in the Caribbean.

    From coral stone houses in Barbados to beach cottages in the Bahamas and stays in St. Barts with incredible sea views, the properties across this region have their own distinct rhythm. Whether you’re looking for a chic modern condo in a vibrant port town or an overwater villa where you can dive straight into the sea, the options are as diverse as the islands themselves. And trust me, there’s something special about having a little taste of the tropics all to yourself. If you're ready to book a trip of your own, read on for my favorite Airbnbs across the Caribbean.

    We've vetted these listings based on Superhost and Guest Favorite status, ratings, amenities, location, previous guest reviews, and decor.

    Number of guests: 8Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 3 bathsWhy we love it: Beachfront terrace, complimentary water sports equipment, shared pool and hot tub.

    It has been revealed that start dreamy mornings right at this gorgeous Grace Bay penthouse by pulling up a stool to the kitchen island while someone makes breakfast, then carrying your coffee onto the covered terrace overlooking the water. This three-bedroom works particularly well for families, with two ocean-facing king bedrooms (plus a third king bedroom with a plush bed that makes up for the lack of view) and more than 2,500 square feet of space to roam. Kayaks, paddleboards, and bicycles are provided for guests, making it easy to get everyone outside and to the ocean. Back home, a shared pool and a hot tub await sandy, sun-tired swimmers.

    Location: Providenciales, Turks and CaicosThings to do nearby: Grace Bay Beach, Regent Village, Royal Turks and Caicos Golf Club.

    Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 2.5 bathsWhy we love it: Private pool, covered terrace with ocean views, well-equipped kitchen.

    Sliding glass doors open onto a large covered terrace and dining space at this contemporary oceanfront villa. The primary suite faces white-sand Cabier Beach and Crochu Harbor, while the second bedroom offers rainforest views. The open-strategy kitchen is a win for home cooks, while the small dipping pool is perfect for keeping kids entertained. Most importantly, the rental is ideally located for exploring the Levera and Bathway beaches to the north, Grand Anse Beach and the capital of St. George's to the south, and the Grand Etang crater lake at the island’s center.

    Location: Crochu, GrenadaThings to do nearby: Cabier Beach, La Sagesse Beach, Mount Carmel Waterfalls.

    Number of guests: 8Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 4 bathsWhy we love it: Infinity pool, sea views from every bedroom, firepit.

    Four couples can happily settle into Villa Larimar without drawing straws for the best view. Every bedroom overlooks the sea and has its own bathroom, while the expansive and open kitchen makes cooking together an appealing prospect. Above Grand Cul-de-Sac’s turquoise lagoon, the terrace has room for long dinners, evenings around the firepit, and afternoons beside the infinity pool. Natural materials and colorful textiles soften the interiors, and the beach is a short walk away.

    Sources indicate that location: Grand Cul-de-Sac, St. BartsThings to do nearby: Grand Cul-de-Sac Beach, kayaking, Lorient Beach.

    Check Availability at Le Collectionist.

    Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Private pool, Lacanche range, outdoor shower.

    This two-bedroom villa on Anse des Cayes Bay comes with serious bragging rights. Recently featured in Elle Decor France, the elegant property has a neutral color palette and blends modern, organic aesthetics with beautiful art and sumptuous furnishings. (Check out that gourmet Lacanche range in the kitchen—swoon!) Guests are treated to sweeping ocean views in every room, but you'll likely want to while away in the hanging bamboo chair or poolside hammock, beach read in hand.

    It has been revealed that location: Anse des Cayes, St. BartsThings to do nearby: Anse des Cayes Beach, St. Jean, Gustavia.

    Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Gorgeous architecture, outdoor shower, cliffside beach access.

    Sources indicate that perched above a secluded beach on Eleuthera’s Atlantic coast, this one-bedroom home is an architectural gem designed by Brillhart Architects with a few magazine features to its name. Built from cedar and thatch, it feels seamlessly connected to the elements, with shutters that frame endless ocean views. Inside, midcentury furnishings and handcrafted details echo the simplicity of its natural setting. This is a retreat for explorers, surfers, and romantics drawn to life’s quieter edges. Catch a wave at Surfer's Beach, hike along the Bluff Trail, or linger in the breeze before watching the stars ignite the sky.

    Location: Near Gregory Town, Eleuthera, BahamasThings to do nearby: Secret Beach, Gregory Town, Surfer’s Beach.

    Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: Studio, 1 bathWhy we love it: Shared courtyard pool, beach access, rental car available for an additional fee.

    In a recent development, tucked along Cable Beach, this boutique escape captures the refined ease of Bahamian coastal living. The studio’s bright interiors feature a king-size bed, designer kitchenette, and spa-style bath. Step outside to a palm-shaded courtyard with a tranquil pool, or wander down to the private beach for a swim in turquoise waters. Restaurants, shops, and the lively Baha Mar resort may only be minutes away, but the property maintains a peaceful and secluded air.

    Location: Cable Beach, Nassau, BahamasThings to do nearby: Cable Beach, Baha Mar restaurants and casino, Baha Bay Water Park.

    Number of guests: 6Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Hot tub, bamboo garden, spacious terraces.

    It has been revealed that art Deco fiends will marvel at the original detailing (those Creole tiles!) in this 1940s Santurce mansion. The lovingly restored three-bedroom has three balconies and two spacious sundecks for watching the people of this historic neighborhood go by. The striking midcentury-modern furnishings look as if they were lifted from a magazine spread, while the abundant houseplants will be the envy of any green thumb. The area is rich with restaurants, bars, and shops, and the nearest beach is reachable in 30 minutes on foot.

    Location: San Juan, Puerto RicoThings to do nearby: Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico, Hacienda San Pedro coffee shop, Santurce galleries.

    Number of guests: 6Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 2.5 bathsWhy we love it: Private infinity pool, sea and mountain views, kitchen with double ovens.

    Past guests have called this three-bedroom property a “paradise in paradise” and “by far the best home we've ever rented.” Tucked away in the mountains of Juana Diaz, Puerto Rico, you'll enjoy both mountain and ocean views, as well as your own private pool and hot tub. If you must work remotely, there's an office to do so, but I'd rather spend time decompressing on the balcony's egg swings or taking a bath in the primary bedroom's freestanding tub.

    Location: Juana Díaz, Puerto RicoThings to do nearby: Juana Díaz town square, Casa Museo de los Santos Reyes, Ponce excursions.

Hosts provide beach chairs, old-school fringed beach umbrellas, and cruiser bikes, which can be checked out at the office; a shared resort-style pool with a heated spa is yours to enjoy, too. The home has room for up to four guests (two adults and two children) with one king bed, one queen-size sleeper sofa, and one bathroom. The in-unit washer/dryer is a nice bonus for those who prefer to head home with a suitcase full of clean clothes.

This two-level penthouse makes it easy to develop a dream-worthy routine for a family gathering. Three king bedrooms face either the sea or the marina, while an upstairs mezzanine bedroom has two double beds. Refreshed in September 2026, the apartment pairs a full kitchen with a terrace grill for outdoor dining. The interior is just as swoon-inducing too, with its high vaulted ceilings and bright white kitchen with four-burner twin stoves.     How many countries are in the Caribbean?

    The Caribbean is a diverse region made up of over 700 islands, islets, reefs, and cays, but not all are independent countries. In total, there are 13 sovereign nations and 17 dependent territories spread across the Caribbean Sea. The independent countries include popular destinations such as Jamaica, the Bahamas, Barbados, St. Lucia, and Trinidad and Tobago. The dependent territories—like Puerto Rico (US), Martinique (France), and the Cayman Islands (UK)—offer a mix of cultural influences and governance structures. While each island varies in size, language, and history, the entire region is united by its tropical climate, vibrant cultures, and rich mix of African, European, and Indigenous heritage.

    What is the best island to visit in the Caribbean?

    There isn’t one “best” Caribbean island—it just depends on what kind of experience you’re seeking. Families often love Jamaica for its all-inclusive resorts, kid-friendly activities, and easy flights from the US. Surfers gravitate toward Barbados and Puerto Rico, which boast consistent swells and a laid-back surf culture. Solo travelers often choose Puerto Rico or Curaçao, thanks to their safety, walkable cities, and friendly locals. For romantic getaways, St. Lucia and Antigua are top picks—think private villas, lush rainforests, and stunning beaches perfect for couples. And for multi-generational trips, the Bahamas or Turks and Caicos stand out, offering luxury accommodations, calm beaches for kids, and plenty of excursions for all ages. Each island has its own rhythm and charm, so the “best” one depends on your travel style and interests.

    When is the best time to travel to the Caribbean?

    It has been revealed that the best time to visit the Caribbean typically falls between December and April, during the region’s dry season. This period offers warm temperatures, low humidity, and minimal rainfall—ideal conditions for beach days and outdoor adventures. However, it’s also the peak tourist season, meaning higher prices and more crowds. For travelers seeking better deals and fewer tourists, the shoulder months of May, June, and November are excellent alternatives, offering good weather with occasional rain showers. The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June to November, and while severe storms are rare on most islands, it’s wise to stay informed about forecasts if traveling during this time.

    Which islands in the Caribbean are the most affordable?

    Recent findings suggest that jamaica and the Dominican Republic are good places to start if you're looking for budget-friendly rentals. But keep in mind that no matter which island you head to, the neighborhood and season you're traveling in matter just as much as anything else, and an exclusive beachfront address can promptly change your budget. To get the most bang for your buck, consider traveling during shoulder or off seasons, and take a look at rentals outside of the typical tourist hot spots.

    Are there any islands in the Caribbean you can visit from the US without a passport?

    Yes. US citizens traveling directly from the mainland can visit Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands without a passport. The US Virgin Islands include St. Thomas, St. John, and St. Croix, and travelers can also head to Puerto Rico’s offshore islands of Vieques and Culebra.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A mother states Delta Air Lines separated her from her two-year-old daughter, then told her to ask other passengers to switch seats.
    • In a Reddit post, a passenger describes trying to resolve separate seat assignments on a flight from Orlando (MCO) to Atlanta (ATL).
    • She says she was directed to the gate for assistance, but received this response:.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A mother states Delta Air Lines separated her from her two-year-old daughter, then told her to ask other passengers to switch seats. She says she had purchased Comfort+ and originally selected seats together. If her account is accurate, this was a problem for Delta to resolve before boarding, not something to leave a parent negotiating in the aisle.

    In a Reddit post, a passenger describes trying to resolve separate seat assignments on a flight from Orlando (MCO) to Atlanta (ATL). She was traveling with her husband, their 2½-year-old daughter, and their one-year-old son.

    She says she was directed to the gate for assistance, but received this response:.

    In a recent development, “I explained that she’s two and cannot sit by herself. Their solution? Tell me it was my responsibility to ask other passengers to switch seats.”.

    Industry observers note that when commenters questioned whether she had purchased basic economy or failed to select seats, she clarified that she had booked Comfort+. After checking her original confirmation, she added:.

    Industry observers note that “I just looked and it was definitely Delta. I have 3 flight / time changes – I originally booked us in 15 D / 15 E / 15 F – we ended up in 15 F / 15 A / 16 A.”.

    This remains her account and we don’t have a way to verify the booking history or the exchange with the gate staff. She also does not clearly state how the family ultimately sat onboard.

    I have traveled extensively with my children, including when they were very young. There is a considerable difference between wanting the entire family together and needing a two-year-old beside a parent.

    Recent findings suggest that it is unreasonable to ask an airline to rearrange a cabin so that every adult in a traveling party can sit together. Heidi and I can sit apart. One parent can sit with one child while the other sits elsewhere with the other child. We have done that many times.

    Recent findings suggest that but a toddler needs an adult who can help with the seatbelt, food, and everything else that comes with flying at that age. The stranger assigned to the adjacent seat cannot reasonably become the person expected to provide that help.

    According to recent reports, I see no excuse for the Delta agent. Once an agent knows a toddler has been assigned a seat away from both parents, someone needs to take responsibility for finding a workable arrangement and it should be someone in a position of authority…like the gate agent.

    I am also sympathetic to passengers who pre-select a seat and then find themselves pressured to move.

    According to recent reports, A parent should not board, occupy someone else’s seat, and announce that the family needs to sit together and a passenger should not be shamed for declining an aisle-to-middle swap. There may be very good reasons that person selected that particular seat, and those reasons are not necessarily anyone else’s business.

    That is precisely why the airline should handle this.

    In a recent development, an agent can review the seat map, identify possible swaps, and ask for volunteers. If necessary, the airline can offer an incentive rather than expect a stranger to absorb the inconvenience for free. There may also be a solution involving a different cabin, provided the family agrees and any fare difference is addressed.

    The ultimate solution to situations like these does not have to preserve every preference the family had when booking. It does need to put a young child beside a responsible adult.

    The published Delta family seating policy states:.

    “Delta strives to seat family members together upon request.”.

    It directs customers who cannot obtain seats together online or through the app to contact reservations to review the available options. That wording is less reassuring than a guarantee. Even so, I would expect the assistance to amount to more than telling a parent to start asking around once onboard.

    Parents should understand fare restrictions and select seats when possible, but a two-year-old’s need to sit beside a parent does not disappear because the family purchased a cheaper ticket and it becomes legally dicey to not sell basic economy tickets to young children. However, in this case it was not a basic economy ticket but a Comfort+ seat.

    Industry observers note that selecting seats months in advance does not mean you can stop checking them. Whenever I receive a schedule change, I review the flights and seat assignments and check again often in the week leading up to travel. Be sure to take a screenshot of your original seat assignments if they were not reflected on your ticket confirmation.

    In a recent development, if a young child becomes separated from a parent, contact the airline promptly and explain the child’s age. If reservations cannot resolve it, arrive early and ask an airport agent…don’t agree to negotiate onboard…it’s unreasonable, even for Frontier Airlines.

    This is called “gardening” your reservation.

    A mother claims Delta assigned her toddler a separate seat and left her to ask other passengers to move, despite originally booking seats together in Comfort+. We have only her account, but the underlying expectation is reasonable: a two-year-old should sit beside a parent, and the airline should help arrange that.

    According to recent reports, other passengers deserve respect for their seat choices too. Resolving the matter before boarding protects everyone from an awkward confrontation that should never have been necessary….

    • French Bee also flies to Newark, Latest Jersey, but Southwest does not offer service there.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Southwest and French Bee are joining forces to expand international travel options for passengers not only on both sides of the Atlantic, but also the Pacific. The two carriers declared a latest interline partnership that will allow travelers to combine flights on both airlines under a single ticket.

    It has been revealed that the agreement connects French Bee’s international network with Southwest’s extensive domestic network in the U.S. The partnership will provide connections through French Bee’s three U.S. gateway airports that Southwest also serves: Los Angeles, Miami, and San Francisco.

    French Bee also flies to Newark, Latest Jersey, but Southwest does not offer service there.

    Passengers will be able to connect between French Bee’s international flights and Southwest domestic flights without having to purchase separate tickets for each airline or recheck bags at each airline.

    French Bee operates an all-Airbus A350 fleet, with its primary hub located at Paris-Orly Airport, and operations to North America and destinations in the Indian Ocean and South Pacific.

    Southwest passengers will gain access to French Bee destinations not only from Paris, but also Tahiti in French Polynesia, which the French carrier flies to from San Francisco. The partnership will also offer one-stop French Bee connections from Paris to the Maldives and Sri Lanka, scheduled to launch in December 2026, along with current flights to Reunion Island.

    In a recent development, for French Bee customers, the latest arrangement provides access to a much larger network of domestic destinations throughout the U.S. Southwest’s network includes cities such as Las Vegas, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Nashville, Austin, San Diego, Phoenix, and multiple destinations in the Hawaiian Islands.

    The agreement represents another step in Southwest’s expanding international connectivity strategy, as the airline continues to develop relationships with overseas carriers rather than rely exclusively on its own international operations with its all-Boeing 737 fleet.

    Tickets for connecting flights are now available through French Bee’s website.
