    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.

    People are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that. Can AI help you find award flights and secure upgrades? It’s something I’d like to study in a bit more detail and write about in the coming weeks, but I just saw a post on Instagram that piqued my interest, so I figured it would make for a fun story. Consider this just a little teaser, for the time being.

    An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface. The idea is simply that ChatGPT helped someone secure an upgrade through the standard means — it’s not like ChatGPT used his/her/their charm to sweet talk someone into an upgrade by dressing up nicely. 😉.

    Let me actually just quote the description of the video, which covers most of the content:.

    What happens when you ask ChatGPT to upgrade your flight to first class?

    I tried this on my flight in two weeks and it actually worked.

    In a recent development, go to ChatGPT and switch from Chat to Work at the top. Start a new chat and give it your airline and confirmation code.

    Prompt 1:“Ask me every question you need about my credit cards, my miles, and my memberships, and map out every upgrade currency I own for this exact flight.”.

    ChatGPT demonstrates you that you’ve been sitting on upgrade power this whole time without even knowing it.

    Prompt 2:“Now look up my exact flight, check how empty the first class cabin is, and tell me every way I can get up there, ranked from free to cheapest.”.

    According to recent reports, prompt 3:“Now go get me the upgrade. Use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.”.

    ChatGPT opens its own browser, logs into your airline, and actually chases that seat for you while you sit back and do nothing.

    You can watch the video for yourself below.

    A post shared by Maverick Maltin | AI & ChatGPT (@mavgpt).

    I don’t want to suggest AI isn’t useful, but I’d say that the example given is actually very poor. First of all, let’s be clear about what’s actually going on here. He had booked a business class ticket on American from Los Angeles (LAX) to London (LHR), and then upgraded to first class.

    Now, in the first place, something isn’t fully accurate here:.

    According to recent reports, okay, maybe he edited the dates, or something, which is fine, and it’s besides the point, but as a detail oriented airline nerd, I couldn’t help but notice those things. Anyway, let’s assume this is all accurate:.

    To me, this is kind of where AI falls flat, and it isn’t the correct way to use it. The prompt was reportedly to “use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.” This is where I get confused — you’d think that AI would be able to scour reviews online, and see that American first class isn’t (well, or wasn’t) really viewed as a product that’s worth the premium.

    If AI were really providing useful advice here, it would’ve recommend waitlisting with the systemwide upgrade, and otherwise recommending the guy save his 70,000 miles, and use them for something else. While there are definitely some strong use cases for AI, I think this is actually a pretty poor showing of what it can do.

    By the way, keep in mind that under United’s updated contract of carriage, using AI to help service reservations is banned, and could potentially get your ticket canceled. Whether there’s any enforcement of that remains to be seen.

    According to recent reports, while the thought of using AI to score an upgrade might sound great, don’t count on it actually getting you the best deal. An AI whiz claims he has the secret to using AI to upgrade to first class. All AI did was use the instant upgrade offer that was available directly on American’s website, and it didn’t even encourage him to skip the upgrade due to it not being worthwhile, or waitlisting the upgrade with a systemwide upgrade, which is objectively a much better deal than 70,000 miles.

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov.
    • According to recent reports, saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen.
    • Industry observers note that democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    According to recent reports, saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen. Bernie Sanders noted Wednesday that he would prioritize passing the universal health care plan if he assumes the chairmanship of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee next year as expected.

    Industry observers note that democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters. And the idea could be buoyed by an influx of progressive lawmakers elected in the midterms.

    In a recent development, sanders noted Medicare for All is gaining support from voters across the country who are looking to overhaul the American health care system as costs have soared. Democrats on the committee will move the legislation “as aggressively as we can, as rapidly as we can,” he said.

    His version, introduced in April and referred to the Senate Finance Committee, would implement the universal health care system over four years. In the first year, the the age of Medicare eligibility would drop to 55 from 65, while coverage would expand to include dental, hearing and vision care. The bill would also provide coverage for eligible children during the first year.

    The age of eligibility would fall another 10 years in each of the following years until the fourth year, when coverage would be extended to all Americans.

    Recent findings suggest that “If there has ever been a time in the modern history of our country . . . to address the crises facing working families, this is that time,” Sanders stated, noting that Democrats will have a 56-44 majority when the 120th Congress begins in January, the largest margin for either party in 16 years.

    Sources indicate that sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., along with nine other Senate Democrats, last week offered an alternative Medicare expansion plan, which would lower the eligibility to those ages 50 and up.

    While who will be leading Senate Democrats is still an open question — Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Charles E. Schumer of Latest York, who has been the top Senate Democrat since 2017 — Sanders stated he is confident the Medicare for All bill will get to the Senate floor, “no matter who the [Senate majority] leader is.” Sanders previously expressed opposition to Schumer leading the conference.

    Asked about efforts to extend the Affordable Care Act enhanced subsidies, Sanders responded he’s “all in.” However, he added “the American people and elected officials understand the current health care system is broken.”.

    Subsidies that help enrollees pay for health care premiums on the ACA exchanges were expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, but these enhanced credits expired at the end of last year, raising costs for many who relied on them to help defray costs.

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, nominated on Wednesday to be speaker next year, previously outlined broader health care priorities such as extending the ACA tax credits and reversing Medicaid cuts enacted in Republicans' reconciliation package last year. When asked Tuesday how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that’s all part of an ongoing conversation.”.

    In addition to expanding Medicare coverage, Sanders reiterated his push to lower prescription drug prices. The Vermont lawmaker previously introduced legislation aimed at reducing the cost of brand name prescription drugs by linking domestic prices to international price benchmarks.

    To enact some of the agenda, Sanders may have to court Republicans.

    According to recent reports, sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., said last week that he plans to serve as the top Republican on the HELP committee next year. Sanders said Wednesday that his likely GOP counterpart “has shown an enormous amount of courage in taking on Republican leadership year after year.”.

    Sanders added that although Paul may have a different viewpoint from himself on committee issues, he looks forward to finding common ground.

    Breaking: Southwest Airlines' New 6-Hour Alaska Route Is Flopping: Here's Why

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (689 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, southwest Airlines has not flown to Alaska for long.
    • Industry observers note that many routes take time to develop, while some perform worse than anticipated despite strong enough expectations.
    • According to recent reports, it is notable to note that data from the US Department of Transportation (DOT) is at the moment only available until the end of August 2026, although that was only half-a-month before the first season's flights from Las Vegas and Anchorage ended.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, southwest Airlines has not flown to Alaska for long. The increasingly evolving hybrid operator's first service to the Last Frontier was on May 15, 2026. Two routes were available from the get-go, with flights from Las Vegas and Denver, both of which are major cities for Southwest.

    Industry observers note that many routes take time to develop, while some perform worse than anticipated despite strong enough expectations. An airline will often be able to tell how well a new link will do within the first couple of days of tickets going on sale. Initial data for Southwest's two markets suggests that one, in particular, might not be doing particularly well.

    According to recent reports, it is notable to note that data from the US Department of Transportation (DOT) is at the moment only available until the end of August 2026, although that was only half-a-month before the first season's flights from Las Vegas and Anchorage ended. As it does not consider the full season, it is not fully comprehensive and is, therefore, perhaps somewhat unfair, especially given Alaska is a brand-fresh state for the airline. Treat it for what it is: a simple snapshot of initial performance.

    Covering 2,002 nautical miles (3,708 km) each way, Southwest ran daily between Las Vegas and Anchorage in the first season. The DOT demonstrates that 26,097 round-trip passengers were transported between May and August. However, the load factor was only 68.7%. That was over ten percentage points lower than the carrier's average load at Las Vegas in the same period.

    Southwest's Overall Las Vegas Load.

    It has been revealed that this is just one part of the pie. What about fares? Cirium's Route Grader Report is right now only available until June 2026, so data provides even less of a view. In the first month-and-a-half of life, this new route had an average fare that was 17% higher than the airline's overall network from Las Vegas, but the distance was virtually double the length.

    When this imbalance is considered, the new route to Alaska had distance-adjusted total revenue per available seat mile of 9.23 US cents, which was by far Southwest's worst result from Sin City. More than just this, it was the airline's fourth-lowest result across its entire network.

    According to recent reports, despite only limited initial data, the DOT indicates that just under a quarter of Southwest's traffic only flew between Las Vegas and Anchorage. They did not fly elsewhere. Despite the carrier's daily service and 'relatively' low fares, it only captured 11% of the local market. In contrast, Alaska Airlines had 79% of it.

    It has been revealed that southwest was massively reliant on those who connected to another flight at Nevada's busiest airport. The overnight service from Anchorage, leaving just before midnight and arriving at about 6:00 AM, is designed for that transfer traffic. Despite this and Southwest's considerable network from Sin City, the early overall load was not good (68.7%).

    The low result was perhaps influenced by launching two routes to Alaska simultaneously, both of which have a similar schedule and both of which focus on connectivity. Analysis reveals that the top ten markets from Anchorage via Las Vegas were Dallas Love, Phoenix, Austin, San Antonio, Sacramento, Salt Lake City, San Diego, Orlando, Ontario, and Albuquerque.

    In a recent development, in 2026, Southwest operated nonstop between May 15 and September 14, with 123 round-trip flights available. In 2027, the first departure of the season will now be on June 3, three weeks later. The final service of the year will be on September 13. In total, 103 movements will exist, down by 16% year-over-year.

    What is more notable is that the equipment has changed, although it is possible that it'll change again. For now, at least, the 175-seat 737 MAX 8 has been replaced by the 137-seat 737-700, contributing to a 34% reduction in seats for sale. Perhaps the MAX 7 will take over. The downgauge means that 14,000+ seats have been removed. Clearly, Southwest is taking big action to achieve stronger fare, yield, and load factor performance next year.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by hours after masked ICE agents stormed the jet bridge of a departing flight to arrest a Mexican national who allegedly had a work permit had overstayed his visa (you know, “the worst of the worst”).
    • In the end, the flight was delayed by hours, as the crew was no longer fit to fly, and the Port of Seattle is outraged.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by hours after masked ICE agents stormed the jet bridge of a departing flight to arrest a Mexican national who allegedly had a work permit had overstayed his visa (you know, “the worst of the worst”). This ended up turning into a huge jet bridge melee, leading to additional arrests, as ICE claims that someone hurled hot coffee at the officers.

    In the end, the flight was delayed by hours, as the crew was no longer fit to fly, and the Port of Seattle is outraged. This is quite the story, as flagged by PYOK.

    This incident happened on the morning of Saturday, November 21, 2026, and involves Alaska Airlines flight AS1306, scheduled to operate from Seattle (SEA) to Los Angeles (LAX).

    This was first reported by a passenger on the flight, who explained that “ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding,” and went on to explain that they were “deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale.”.

    Industry observers note that ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding. Now deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale @CNN @nytimes @seattletimes.

    Video taken from the jet bridge shows masked ICE agents trying to arrest people on the jet bridge.

    Masked ICE agents detained two people on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers were boarding a flight. Alaska Airlines remarked ICE officers gave them no advance notice of the operation. pic.twitter.com/r44WPTvGdv.

    As a result of this incident, the Alaska flight ended up being delayed by hours. It was initially supposed to depart at 8:10AM and arrive at 11:01AM, but instead, departed at 11:03AM and arrived at 1:36PM.

    Here’s how ICE explained its actions:.

    It has been revealed that on November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws.

    During the arrest other travelers began to obstruct and assault our law enforcement officers—a federal crime and a felony. One passenger hurled hot coffee on the officers. Other passengers began obstructing federal officers.

    In a recent development, the individual who threw the hot coffee was identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, an illegal alien from Mexico and visa overstay. She was subsequently arrested as well. She will be charged with assaulting a federal officer.

    Assaulting and obstructing law enforcement is a crime and a felony. Secretary Mullin has been clear: anyone who assaults or obstructs law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the fullest extent of the law. Our brave law enforcement is facing more than a 1,600% increase in assaults, 3,300% increase in vehicular attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them. This violence must end.

    Industry observers note that on November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws. During the arrest other travelers began to… https://t.co/nXiBxAqIJ5.

    The Port of Seattle expressed its outrage about the incident, releasing the following statement:.

    In a recent development, we are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles. Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge. The Port has continually asked, and local federal immigration authorities have previously agreed to protocols at SEA, and we are in conversation with DHS on whether any of these protocols were breached. However, the Port remains committed to the safety of all of our travelers and staff and airline team. This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred.

    Washington Governor Bob Ferguson was also angry, as he held a press conference about what happened, and released the following statement:.

    Industry observers note that ICE is completely and totally out of control. Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities. Today’s actions at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport are just the latest example of ICE’s deeply un-American tactics. I’ll have more to say this afternoon.

    Meanwhile Alaska Airlines took a more toned down approach, and just expressed “concern,” releasing the following statement:.

    Sources indicate that we are concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306. We recognize how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests. Alaska Airlines is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials. We do not direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity, and we remain committed to protecting the privacy and safety of our guests and employees wherever possible.

    There’s simply no arguing that in terms of public sentiment, the tides have turned in terms of immigration enforcement, with even Trump recently admitting “I think it might be too tough.”.

    Industry observers note that Q: You think your deportation policy went too far?Trump: I think it might be too tough. pic.twitter.com/NKhFjZKxnd.

    No matter how you feel about deportations as such, having them go down in this way for someone who simply overstayed their visa is a step too far, in my opinion. I mean, it’s one thing if we’re talking about a violent criminal on some sort of watch list, but that’s clearly not the case here.

    Our four-year-old is currently at the age where he asks “why” in response to everything… and he has a lot of good questions that often make me step back and think “oh, that’s a good point.” I put myself in the situation of being on the jet bridge here as a parent, and trying to explain what was going on.

    And here’s the thing — it’s one thing if these people were in uniform and identifying themselves, but when you have people who refuse to identify themselves, it’s an especially bad look.     • A new deal with Miami-Dade County will help American Airlines solidify and eventually expand its maintenance operations at Miami International Airport.
    • The county unveiled this week that it will buy a hangar and maintenance space at Miami International from a third-party owner and lease it directly to American for its MRO operations.
    • Sources indicate that according to the Miami Herald, American already leases the property and uses it for maintenance work, but a change in ownership from private jet operator Aero Miami to the county will give American more leeway to develop the space as it sees fit.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A new deal with Miami-Dade County will help American Airlines solidify and eventually expand its maintenance operations at Miami International Airport.

    The county unveiled this week that it will buy a hangar and maintenance space at Miami International from a third-party owner and lease it directly to American for its MRO operations. The acquisition includes Hangar 890, Building 891, 10.2 acres of land, and a 2.2-acre parking lot.

    Sources indicate that according to the Miami Herald, American already leases the property and uses it for maintenance work, but a change in ownership from private jet operator Aero Miami to the county will give American more leeway to develop the space as it sees fit. The fresh lease with the county will run for 20 years and cost American $67.8 million, the newspaper said.

    The airline plans to keep more than 650 aircraft maintenance workers at the facility. It has also agreed to complete about $13.9 million in building repairs.

    “Miami is a cornerstone of American’s international network and a consequential part of our long-term growth strategy,” American Senior Vice President of Miami Operations Juan Carlos Liscano remarked in a news release. “This agreement reinforces our dedication to our Miami team and preserves our ability to continue growing our network to more destinations around the world for our customers.”.

    American is the largest airline at Miami, carrying more than half of all passengers there.

    Tech Report: Restored to Calder’s blueprint, the clouds are spinning again

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1154 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday.
    • The day after Alexander Calder presented his blueprint for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.
    • Rower felt a sense of awe as he stared up at his grandfather’s work, finally restored to what he had envisioned.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    The day after Alexander Calder presented his blueprint for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.

    Fifty years later, Alexander S.C. Rower felt a sense of awe as he stared up at his grandfather’s work, finally restored to what he had envisioned.

    Industry observers note that “It’s totally phenomenal,” he stated, pointing up at the now-moving clouds as he spoke, spinning his finger around. “It’s not entertainment, but it’s trying to emulate naturalness, trying to emulate what nature would do.”.

    It was a long time coming for Rower, who remembers traveling to the Capitol in his 20s for the original dedication of the Mountains and Clouds sculpture in 1987. The mobile portion stopped rotating as Calder intended in the 1990s, and it was ultimately removed in 2014 after being deemed unsafe by the Architect of the Capitol. Millions of dollars in private philanthropy later, Calder’s clouds are spinning again.

    It has been revealed that rower was back on the Hill on Wednesday for an event celebrating the restoration, joining Architect of the Capitol Thomas Austin, Sens. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., Angus King, I-Maine, and James Lankford, R-Okla., and the project’s donors. As the speakers addressed the crowd, the clouds began to speed up slightly. Onlookers gathered on the balconies overlooking the atrium and peeked through office windows. Attendees left with tote bags emblazoned with images of Calder’s art.

    According to Rower, who leads the Calder Foundation dedicated to preserving and interpreting his grandfather’s art, the mobile is rotating on a 15-hour cycle that is “totally variable.”.

    “It can go a little faster; it can go a little slower,” he said. “I told the team today that during lunchtime, I want it to speed up just a little bit because everyone’s going to lunch. There’ll be … a lot of activity passing through, and then right at 2:30, well, let’s make it go quieter.”.

    It was a labor of love for those involved, and not an inexpensive one. Jon and Kim Shirley funded the $12 million restoration. Because the pieces were so large, they were transported on an extra-wide load truck and driven at a speed of 35 miles per hour from Michigan.

    “We had to call every senator or governor that we knew on that route, which went through seven states, to get permissions,” he stated. “That was a huge thing to overcome, and it all happened over a weekend. So my wife was actually on the phone with a governor’s wife on Saturday evening. The next day, he called up his Department of Transportation and got a permit.”.

    Christian Quilici, who helped manage the project on behalf of the Shirleys and said he serves as a liaison between the foundation and Congress, said the hardest part of the project was the size of it.

    Industry observers note that “We had to tear the wall down on C Street, which nobody really thought of in the beginning,” he stated. “Nobody got how major this was until it indicated up on their doorstep.”.

    Quilici stated he spent years educating at least 30 different senators about the quest to reunite the mobile with the stationary mountains left behind. Some of the biggest champions were seated in the front row at Wednesday’s event, including Senate Democratic Whip Richard J. Durbin. Absent was Sen. Christopher S. Murphy, D-Conn., who has been away from the Capitol while recovering from a stroke but has been a supporter of the sculpture’s restoration for years, pressing former acting Architect of the Capitol Joseph DiPietro on it at a 2024 Senate Legislative Branch Appropriations budget hearing.

    “Is there any chance that before I leave the Senate, or at least before I die, we can get the clouds back up there?” Murphy said at the time.

    Padilla read a letter on Wednesday from Murphy, whose state was Calder’s home for much of his life.

    “This statue is actually a statement on our democracy, that we have substantial pieces of monumental art right in the middle of our most key and most iconic government buildings. To get this piece of art restored to how it was designed by the artist, well, that’s good for Connecticut. But I also like to think … it’s good for democracy too,” Murphy’s statement said.

    The restoration was funded entirely by donations from the Shirleys, who are prominent Calder collectors, according to Rower.

    In a recent development, “It’s very emotional to see the work completed after 10 years of us working so hard with the Architect of the Capitol and Calder Foundation. It’s a very overpowering, overwhelming emotion,” mentioned Kim Shirley.

    In addition to helping fund the project, she’s a former Senate staffer who worked in Hart before Calder’s work was installed. Years after her time in the Senate was over, her husband Jon wanted to show her the sculpture, now filling the space she used to walk through every day.

    It has been revealed that but when the two arrived, the clouds weren’t hanging from the ceiling like they were supposed to be. He called up Rower, who was a friend of his, and remarked he wanted to get them back to how Calder intended. On Wednesday, the three of them stood together in Hart, looking up.

    Technological and engineering advancements allowed for newer, lighter clouds to be built and be safe to hang from the ceiling.

    “Before it was like a bulb, it looked like a hoagie sandwich, and now it looks just really sharp, like a razor cutting through space, which was Calder’s intention,” Rower remarked.

    According to Rower, it involved laser-measuring the original model of Mountains and Clouds sitting in a glass case nearby in the Hart atrium. The upcoming clouds, he mentioned, are made of carbon fiber.

    “These are giant things up in the air, and they’re just so gentle and subtle,” he mentioned.

    Recent findings suggest that younger Hill staffers don’t know a time with clouds. But for those who have spent decades in the building, it was a special moment to see them spin, as Lankford told the crowd.

    “I can’t tell you how many tour groups that I’ve walked through this building and I pointed to this, and I stated it’s only half there, and would take them over to the little model that’s right over here, and say this is what it’s supposed to look like,” said the senator, a former Hill staffer himself.

    Standing under his grandfather’s sculpture, Rower found himself quoting the man responsible for it all.

    “I find that everything I do, if it is made for a particular spot, is more successful,” he noted, gazing up at it.

    The Billion-Dollar Companies Behind Half Of The World's Commercial Aircraft

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1608 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, ethan is an aviation professional with a degree in Aviation Management with Flight from the Florida Institute of Technology.
    • He at the moment holds a Restricted ATP and Commercial Multi‑Engine Pilot certificate and works in aviation supply chain and aircraft component repair.
    • A lifelong aviation enthusiast, Ethan spent countless hours at Raleigh–Durham International Airport’s observation deck studying air traffic and practicing amateur photography and videography.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, ethan is an aviation professional with a degree in Aviation Management with Flight from the Florida Institute of Technology. He previously wrote aviation and tourism features for Florida Tech’s student newspaper, The Crimson, where he developed a clear, reader‑focused reporting style. Aviation journalism has remained a consistent priority throughout his career.

    He at the moment holds a Restricted ATP and Commercial Multi‑Engine Pilot certificate and works in aviation supply chain and aircraft component repair. Alongside his industry role, he is pursuing his Certified Flight Instructor rating and actively building flight experience.

    A lifelong aviation enthusiast, Ethan spent countless hours at Raleigh–Durham International Airport’s observation deck studying air traffic and practicing amateur photography and videography.

    It has been revealed that while household names such as United Airlines and Lufthansa dominate the skies in terms of fleet count, there are many companies in existence that have similarly sized fleets that do not carry passengers or cargo, nor do they operate charter missions. These companies never sell a ticket, operate a route, or pursue significant branding campaigns.

    According to recent reports, some of these firms control fleets worth tens of billions of dollars, and one owns more aircraft than many of the airlines the public recognizes. The airline industry is composed primarily of two main financial systems: ownership and lease.

    In a recent development, many companies such as Delta Air Lines are known for owning a high percentage of their fleet, notably their older Boeing 717 or Boeing 767 fleets. However, the majority of airlines lease a portion of their jets, as many aircraft with long order backlogs at the manufacturer itself can be hard to obtain. Leasing is a common way to bypass delivery delays.

    Most people assume airlines buy the aircraft they fly. Increasingly, that is not the case. According to the International Air Transport Association (IATA), leasing now accounts for more than half of the world's commercial fleet, making aircraft leasing one of the most important yet least visible sectors in aviation.

    According to recent reports, rather than purchasing aircraft outright, many airlines rent them under long-term agreements from specialized leasing companies. The scale of those firms is difficult to appreciate until their fleets are examined. AerCap, the world's largest aircraft lessor, reported owning 1,501 aircraft and managing another 148 at the end of 2025, with an additional 283 aircraft on order.

    Those figures make AerCap a larger aircraft owner than many of the world's biggest airlines. Meanwhile, competitors such as SMBC Aviation Capital, Avolon, BOC Aviation, and Air Lease Corporation collectively control thousands more aircraft worth hundreds of billions of dollars.

    However, ownership and operation are not the same thing. If airlines do not own many of the aircraft they fly, why would they willingly hand that responsibility to someone else? While there are many sides to the discussion, the answer relates to the complexities of operating an airplane to begin with, which is far more involved than car or boat ownership, for example.

    According to recent reports, A upcoming Boeing 787-9 carries a list price exceeding $300 million, while even narrowbody aircraft represent investments worth tens of millions of dollars each. Purchasing hundreds of aircraft outright would require enormous amounts of capital that airlines often prefer to dedicate elsewhere. Dry leasing is the most common and most cost-effective way to accomplish this cost benefit.

    Recent findings suggest that aircraft leasing allows airlines to expand fleets without making the full upfront purchase themselves. Instead, leasing firms acquire aircraft from manufacturers such as Boeing and Airbus and lease them to airlines over periods that frequently range from six to twelve years. Airlines gain access to modern aircraft while preserving cash and reducing financial risk.

    Aircraft Owned/Managed (2025-2026).

    United Mainline + Regional Fleet.

    Hundreds of owned and investor-serviced aircraft.

    Hundreds of owned aircraft and major order book.

    While having direct operating authority of 1,066 aircraft, United Airlines' fleet also includes a subsection of leased aircraft, according to the SEC. This figure comprises 958 owned and 108 leased, at the end of 2025. This number is significantly less than AerCap's total number of active leases, which, on paper, causes AerCap to resemble a major international airline.

    Sources indicate that in practice, passengers rarely notice that a different tech giant owns the aircraft they are flying on. Under a dry lease, the lessor provides the aircraft while the airline supplies its own pilots, maintenance program, insurance, and operating certificates. To passengers, the aircraft appears no different from any other jet in the airline's fleet.

    Sources indicate that one recent example comes from Avolon's reported October 2025 sale-and-leaseback agreement with TAAG Angola Airlines involving 787-9 aircraft. In that arrangement, the aircraft are operated by TAAG, but ownership remains with the leasing tech giant. Similar transactions occur throughout the industry and frequently involve new aircraft deliveries from Boeing and Airbus. An aircraft may spend its entire operational life flying for airlines that never technically own it.

    Recent findings suggest that A wet lease is an entirely different form of leasing, provided by companies like Heston Airlines, Hi Fly, or Wamos Air. The aircraft is frequently in the livery of the lessor, although not always. Further, the in-flight service, cabin crew, and standards are all those of the lessor organization. Wet leases generally have a higher cost than dry leases, and are generally shorter in term.

    The influence of lessors extends far beyond simple ownership. Because companies such as AerCap, Avolon, and SMBC Aviation Capital place enormous aircraft orders, they have become some of Boeing's and Airbus' most crucial customers. Lessors routinely order aircraft years before identifying the airlines that will eventually operate them.

    This purchasing power became especially significant during recent supply chain constraints. CAPA reports that aircraft shortages and production delays have strengthened lessors' market positions by increasing aircraft values and lease rates. Airlines seeking growth often cannot wait years for newly introduced direct deliveries, making leased aircraft one of the few available solutions.

    The result is that lessors frequently influence what aircraft manufacturers build, how quickly airlines can expand, and even which carriers gain access to modern fleets. A major leasing organization may place an order measured in hundreds of aircraft, a scale that rivals the purchasing power of many national airlines.

    Orders placed by airlines themselves to manufacturers such as Boeing or Airbus are typically more noteworthy. They represent a larger upfront financial commitment and a known destination for production aircraft. Orders placed by lessors are less noteworthy, but still significant from an operational standpoint.

    According to recent reports, while the end user of the aircraft is not known when, for example, AerCap placed an order for 100 Airbus jets, such an order boosts the inventory of a lessor. This not only provides options for customers, but an entirely different, and at times, more accessible way of expanding a fleet.

    According to recent reports, the growing importance of lessors is increasingly tied to aircraft scarcity. Airbus and Boeing continue to work through substantial backlogs measured in thousands of aircraft. For airlines needing capacity sooner rather than later, leasing companies often represent the fastest available path to fleet growth.

    Leasing companies also offer smaller airlines and startup carriers alike a lower barrier to entry to operation than buying an aircraft outright from the producer. AerCap provides one of the clearest examples. The organization website published an order book of 283 aircraft entering 2026 while simultaneously managing thousands of aviation assets, including engines and helicopters.

    That position effectively allows it to act as a bridge between manufacturers producing aircraft and airlines seeking them. Manufacturers in the aviation industry have the greatest amount of market control for their product. However, some of that power can be relinquished when a customer also acts as a distributor. The relationship between the manufacturer and the lessor creates an unusual balance of power.

    Manufacturers remain responsible for designing and producing aircraft, but the largest lessors have amassed order books so large that they have become some of Airbus' and Boeing's most crucial customers. Companies such as AerCap regularly place orders measured in the hundreds of aircraft, allowing them to negotiate from a position of strength while shaping fleet decisions across dozens of airlines simultaneously.

    Recent findings suggest that the future significance of aircraft lessors will likely depend on one simple metric: access to aircraft. Airlines can only grow as quickly as upcoming aircraft become available, and both Airbus and Boeing continue to hold order backlogs extending years into the future. Major aircraft manufacturers, while experiencing high backlogs of orders and record customer interest, can lose control of the end use of their product when lessors place massive orders.

    Industry observers note that that reality places unusual attention on companies such as AerCap, Avolon, and SMBC Aviation Capital. Their order books, delivery positions, and financing capabilities may determine which airlines can launch fresh routes, replace aging fleets, or enter emerging markets first.

    In an industry built around aircraft availability, the companies holding the keys to future deliveries may become as important as the carriers operating them. The next major test will come as manufacturers work through production constraints and thousands of aircraft presently sitting in order backlogs move toward delivery.

    In a recent development, whether airlines continue shifting toward leased fleets or return to greater ownership could depend on how effectively Boeing and Airbus satisfy demand over the remainder of the decade. For passengers, the aircraft parked at the gate will probably continue wearing airline colors. The more interesting question is whether the real power behind those fleets increasingly belongs to companies whose names never appear on the boarding pass.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that rakuten is my favorite online shopping portal, and if you’re not using it, you’re leaving rewards on the table. Through December 31, 2026, if you join Rakuten through a qualifying referral link and spend $50 within the first 90 days, you’ll receive a $50 bonus. The person referring you can also receive $50. This is even an opportunity to earn Amex Membership Rewards points or Bilt Points at a very favorable ratio.

    Taking advantage of this Rakuten sign-up bonus is truly a no-brainer, as I’d view this as a way to get $50 worth of stuff for (basically) free. For that matter, you’re missing out more broadly if you’re not earning additional rewards for your online shopping, beyond what you earn with your credit card.

    In this post I’d like to go over all the details of Rakuten, including how the Rakuten referral bonus works, and the easiest way to maximize it (as it’s really easy to take advantage of, even if you don’t think you have an immediate purchase in mind).

    Link: Sign-up for a Rakuten account with a best-ever $50 bonus.

    Rakuten is a free online shopping and rewards platform that pays consumers either cash back or points for the shopping they do online. Rakuten partners with over 3,500 online retailers, many of which are well known, ranging from Lowe’s, to Nike, to Target. The Rakuten shopping portal concept is simple — if you click through from Rakuten to the partner website, Rakuten tracks the purchase and gets paid a commission, and then you get a reward as well.

    Sources indicate that note that as a consumer, Rakuten is free to use. The commission is paid by the business, so you’ll pay the same price you’d pay if you just went directly to the retailer’s website. To maximize your savings, you can even download the Rakuten browser extension, which will automatically notify you when you can earn extra rewards.

    In a recent development, I should mention that there are several online shopping portals out there to choose from, so Rakuten isn’t the only one. Personally I find that Rakuten is my favorite because it has among the largest selection of partners, it gives you the flexibility to earn cash back or points, and I also find the earnings rates to be very competitive.

    It can always pay to use a site like Cashback Monitor to compare the earnings rates for retailers across portals, so that you’re maximizing your rewards. In some situations you may be better off using other portals, so it’s always worth understanding what your options are.

    Through December 31, 2026, Rakuten is offering a generous elevated refer-a-friend bonus. Specifically, if you refer a friend to Rakuten and they spend $50 within the first 90 days, then both the person referring and the person being referred each receive $50.

    This is truly a best-ever bonus, as we’ve previously only seen a bonus of up to $40 — though admittedly this offer has stuck around for quite some time.

    This is a very good deal. Essentially Rakuten is giving out $100 total for a $50 purchase, between the person referring and the person being referred. Long term you can potentially get even more value with Rakuten, as rewards can be converted into Amex or Bilt Points.

    Actually earning the $50 Rakuten sign-up bonus is really straightforward:.

    What’s the timeline with which you’ll actually receive the rewards? With Rakuten you’re paid (either in cash or points) once quarterly, and there’s a cutoff for payments, per the below chart.

    Rakuten partners with literally thousands of retailers, and an eligible purchase worth at least $50 with any eligible retail partner would qualify. When you click over to the partner site, just make sure you keep an eye on any exclusions, since some types of purchases may not qualify for rewards.

    Recent findings suggest that there are also often amazing opportunities to earn up to 100% back or 100x points with select retailers, which is a rate at which I’d gladly buy points all day long, without even factoring in the service being sold. So I take advantage of these deals all the time, even if I don’t actually value the product.

    In a recent development, if you’re not interested in that and don’t have anything you need to buy right now, there’s another creative option. There are easy ways to unlock the $50 bonus, including simply purchasing a $50 gift card through giftcards.com. This is so easy — you can pick up a $50 gift card with a variety of retailers, and then you’ll receive $50 in cash.

    To briefly explain that process, you’d enter giftcards.com in the search bar at the top of Rakuten’s website.

    Then click the “Shop Now” button, which will take you to giftcards.com. All your purchases while on that site will automatically be tracked.

    The website sells a variety of gift cards with popular retailers, including DoorDash, Uber, Delta, Southwest, Hulu, Netflix, Dominos, and many more.

    For example, you could buy a $50 DoorDash gift card at face value, and the code will be delivered by email within minutes.

    Once the purchase is complete, you should see Rakuten automatically tracking the purchase.

    In a recent development, within an hour the purchase should be fully reflected — the Rakuten account will show a credit in the amount of the sign-up bonus, plus the rewards for the actual purchase (which will vary based on whether you choose to earn cash or points). As a standard, giftcards.com offers either 1% cash back, or one point per dollar spent, but sometimes we see increased offers (like right now).

    Taking advantage of this is the obvious choice, in my opinion:.

    The reason that Rakuten is my favorite shopping portal is because Rakuten rewards can be converted into Amex Membership Rewards points or Bilt Rewards points. The exact way this works depends on the currency you choose to earn.

    Sources indicate that with the Rakuten and Amex Membership Rewards partnership, you can consistently earn one point in lieu of one cent, assuming you have an Amex card that earns Membership Rewards points. So if a retailer offers 10% cash back, you can instead earn 10x Amex points.

    Recent findings suggest that based on my latest points valuations, Amex Membership Rewards points are worth 1.7 cents each, because of all the ways there are to redeem the points for first and business class international travel, while getting outsized value. To me that increases the value of the rewards by 70%.

    It has been revealed that this just requires changing one setting in your account, so it’s super easy. The only thing to be aware of is that this points earning opportunity doesn’t apply to the welcome bonus, but does apply to all spending beyond that.

    Industry observers note that that’s not the only opportunity, though. The Rakuten and Bilt Rewards partnership lets members earn Bilt Rewards points in lieu of cash back. Bilt elite members can earn one point in lieu of every one cent, while non-elite members can earn one point in lieu of every two cents. Much like Amex Membership Rewards points, I also value Bilt Rewards points at 1.7 cents each, as there are also many good uses of this points currency.

    What’s cool here is that your cash back can retroactively be converted into Bilt Points for the entire Rakuten “payout” period (roughly quarterly), and that means even the refer-a-friend bonus can be converted into points.

    If you have the choice between one Amex point or one Bilt point, I think many people might prefer the latter, given the value of the rewards, plus how hard they are to earn. However, if the ratio isn’t one point per cent, then I’d go with the Amex partnership instead.

    Beyond the rewards you earn directly with Rakuten, your spending with retailers can of course also earn credit card rewards.

    Rakuten’s co-branded Amex card is among the best cards for Rakuten spending, as it earns 4% cash back on those purchases, on up to $10,000 per calendar year. Beyond that, purchases with online retailers typically don’t qualify for any exciting bonus categories, so most consumers will want to use one of the best cards for everyday spending.

    #100250. Progressive advocates call on House Democrats to force Cuba vote

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (872 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Progressive advocates call on House Democrats to force Cuba vote

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Velázquez, D-N.Y., is the sponsor of a Cuba war powers resolution filed in May.
    • Progressive advocates are urging House Democrats to force a vote during the lame-duck session on a resolution aimed at preventing war against Cuba, arguing the glitch is too urgent to wait until Democrats control the chamber next year.
    • In a recent development, “The Cuban people are suffering and dying, and cannot afford further months of inaction,” 50 progressive groups wrote to Democratic House leaders in a letter dated Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, D-N.Y., is the sponsor of a Cuba war powers resolution filed in May. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Progressive advocates are urging House Democrats to force a vote during the lame-duck session on a resolution aimed at preventing war against Cuba, arguing the glitch is too urgent to wait until Democrats control the chamber next year.

    In a recent development, “The Cuban people are suffering and dying, and cannot afford further months of inaction,” 50 progressive groups wrote to Democratic House leaders in a letter dated Wednesday. “In the midterm elections, U.S. voters resoundingly rejected a foreign policy of war and domination, and made clear their desire for Congress to act forcefully to rein in the Trump administration.

    Holding a vote would demonstrate that Democrats recognize the urgency facing the Cuban people, and would help set the tone for an assertive agenda of peace, diplomacy and respect for international law in the 120th Congress, the letter added.

    Recent findings suggest that at issue is a war powers resolution introduced in May by Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, D-N.Y., and House Foreign Affairs Committee ranking member Rep. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., that would call on the president “to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Cuba, unless explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a specific authorization for use of military force.”.

    The letter was sent to House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries of Latest York, Meeks and House Rules Committee ranking member Jim McGovern, D-Mass. It was signed by prominent anti-war groups such as Win Without War, Just Foreign Policy, the Friends Committee on National Legislation, Indivisible and Code Pink.

    It has been revealed that advocates are frustrated that House Democrats have not forced a vote on a Cuba war powers resolution even as they have forced multiple war powers votes on Iran and see it as an example of leadership that is at odds with the progressive wing of the party. One advocate who requested anonymity to speak candidly said it’s their understanding Democratic leaders are hesitant to make potentially vulnerable Florida members of the caucus vote on the issue.

    Spokespeople for Jeffries and Meeks did not respond to requests for comment Wednesday on whether Democrats will force a vote before the end of the year, what their reasoning is if they don’t and whether they plan to bring up a vote next year.

    Senate Democrats sought to force a vote on a similar resolution earlier this year, but Republicans in that chamber successfully derailed the effort. Senate Republicans raised a point of order that the resolution was not entitled to privileged status under the War Powers Resolution since U.S. troops aren't actively engaged in combat against Cuba. The point of order was sustained in a mostly party-line vote of 51-47.

    Senate Democrats later introduced another Cuba war powers resolution, which they have not tried to force a vote on and have not signaled they will do so before the end of the year.

    The resolutions have come amid several veiled threats from President Donald Trump suggesting eventual military action against Cuba.

    “I want to get Cuba done before I leave,” Trump told conservative radio host Hugh Hewitt last week when asked if he would order the use of military force against Cuba.

    “Frankly, I’d love to be able to do it for the people, for the Cubans that came and were treated really badly, and they came to America,” Trump said, adding he would “certainly consider” taking military action.

    According to recent reports, trump’s comments are on top of a pressure campaign his administration has been waging against Cuba. Since January, the United States has imposed a blockade of oil shipments to the island, causing fuel shortages that have led to lengthy blackouts and aggravated an economic crisis.

    While the Senate vote in April did not go Democrats’ way, advocates still saw it as sending a strong message.

    It has been revealed that “Despite falling short of the majority, this was among the strongest votes in congressional history against the use of blockades, and one of the most important stands Congress has taken against U.S. economic sanctions toward Cuba in over six decades,” the letter from progressive organizations remarked. “The House should take a similarly forceful action at this crucial moment.”.

    The House vote, even if successful, would be largely symbolic since the measure Democrats can force a vote on is a concurrent resolution. Concurrent resolutions are widely considered to be nonbinding even if cleared by both chambers of Congress since they do not get a presidential signature, though anti-war advocates dispute that applies to war powers.

    The progressive groups in their letter called for “decisive leadership” in forcing a vote on the issue.

    It has been revealed that “Across the political spectrum,” the letter said, “Americans do not want another regime change war, nor an open-ended, nation-building project abroad based on false pretenses — especially not when escalation risks exposing the United States to fresh national security risks, placing US servicemembers in harm’s way, stoking regional instability, and becoming the latest chapter in a long history of harmful U.S. regional policies that have fueled mass migration to U.S. shores.”.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus where you’ll get 90,000 bonus points after you make $6,000 or more in purchases within the first 90 days of opening your account. This is the best publicly available bonus that we’ve ever seen on the card, and you can find the bonus offer history in this post.

The good news is that eligibility for this card is unrelated to having any other Atmos Rewards card, so you’re eligible for this card (including the bonus) if you have the Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card (learn more) or Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more).

    Let me emphasize that you are eligible for this product if you have any of the previously issued personal or business HawaiianMiles Barclays cards, or any of the previously issued personal Alaska Mileage Initiative cards.

While Bank of America has the 2/3/4 rule and 3/12 rules, those apply to personal cards, and not business cards. Generally those with a Bank of America banking relationship also have the best odds of approval (though it’s by no means a requirement).

    There’s not a consistent credit score you need to have to be approved for this card, though personally I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

    Applying for this card won’t count as a further card toward Chase’s 5/24 limit, in case that’s a limit you’re trying to stay under.

    Sources indicate that the Atmos Rewards Business Card has bonus categories that can help you rack up points faster. Furthermore, spending on the card can help you earn Atmos Rewards elite status. Let’s talk about how rewarding spending on the card can be.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Air New Zealand has been looking to return to the UK market for some time.
    • That being said, for the upcoming summer 2027 season, the Latest Zealand flag carrier had sought to secure slots at Heathrow.
    • According to recent reports, air Newly introduced Zealand had been flying to London for several decades.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Air New Zealand has been looking to return to the UK market for some time. The last time we saw its black-and-white livery was in March 2020, when it operated its final flight from London Heathrow Airport (LHR) to Auckland International Airport (AKL). Since then, passengers traveling between the UK and New Zealand have had to rely on connecting flights through hubs in the Middle East, Asia or Australia.

    That being said, for the upcoming summer 2027 season, the Latest Zealand flag carrier had sought to secure slots at Heathrow. According to Airport Coordination Limited's (ACL) Initial Coordination Report for London Heathrow, the Star Alliance member requested 434 slots for the season. However, none of these were approved.

    According to recent reports, air Newly introduced Zealand had been flying to London for several decades. The airline initially served London Gatwick Airport (LGW) from Auckland, with stops in Papeete, Tahiti, and Los Angeles. In 1994, it moved its operations to Heathrow, where it continued to fly via Los Angeles. Between 2006 and 2013, the airline also offered flights via Hong Kong.

    Sources indicate that however, the Star Alliance member eventually decided to discontinue its London service due to low passenger numbers. It is unclear what routing it would have used had it secured the slots for summer 2027. Los Angeles appears to have been one possibility, as a spokesperson previously told Simple Flying that the airline would most likely operate the service via the US city using Boeing 777 aircraft.

    According to recent reports, interestingly, Air Latest Zealand had also applied for slots at London Gatwick for the previous summer season and was actually successful in securing them. However, the airline never debuted the flights, as it was facing aircraft availability complications at the time. Up to four of its 14 Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners were grounded simultaneously due to problems with Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 engines and maintenance delays.

    In a recent development, these aircraft have since returned to service. Nevertheless, aircraft availability remains a concern. According to ch-aviation, Air Latest Zealand currently has nine 777-300ERs and 16 787-9s, although only 11 of the latter are in active service. The airline is also awaiting deliveries of three additional 787-9s and five 787-10s, with its outstanding Dreamliner orders expected to be fulfilled by 2028.

    However, Boeing has faced difficulties increasing 787 production to its target of ten aircraft per month, partly due to supply-chain delays involving General Electric GEnx engines. These complications have affected deliveries to customers, including Air Newly introduced Zealand, although planespotters.net data shows that the airline received two Dreamliners in October 2026.

    In a recent development, apart from upcoming aircraft deliveries, the Star Alliance member is also refurbishing its existing widebody fleet. As of late October, 13 of its 14 787-9s had completed cabin upgrades, which include replacing the older inward-facing Business Premier seats with private suites, updating Economy cabins and introducing bunk-style sleeping pods on selected aircraft.

    Sources indicate that the final Dreamliner is expected to return to service before the end of the year. The airline is also scheduled to begin refurbishing its 777 fleet in March 2027. All of which are expected to undergo the upgrades by the end of 2027, meaning aircraft will need to be temporarily withdrawn from service while the work takes place.

    According to recent reports, the exact reason why Air New Zealand did not receive any slots has not been confirmed. However, Heathrow is one of the most slot-constrained airports in the world, and securing additional slots is difficult. According to ACL's report, airlines requested a total of 26,832 slots for summer 2027, but only 151 were allocated, just 0.6% of the requests.

    In a recent development, xiamen Air, which recently launched a weekly service between Xiamen and Heathrow, received most of the approved slots. However, several other airlines were unsuccessful. These included Alaska Airlines, which only began flying to Heathrow from Seattle in May and requested 434 slots for next summer. Emirates also failed to secure any of the 1,920 slots it requested, while Virgin Atlantic, Delta Air Lines, Air India and Riyadh Air were denied all 1,798, 556, 1,736 and 868 slots they sought, respectively.

    The real-world value of choosing the right credit cards for your everyday spending We frequently tout the incredible value you can get from top rewards credit cards — from bonus categories to welcome offers, lucrative benefits to monthly statement credits.

    But exactly how much value can you get from matching the right credit cards to your spending habits?

    Well, we recently set out to answer this very question.

    We challenged three American households with a simple question: Can you make the money you’re already spending work harder for you?

    The answer was a resounding yes.

    Mollie and Kevin were up first. The pair recently moved in together ahead of their wedding, and they’re working through how to combine their finances while also saving for their dream honeymoon to Thailand and Vietnam. Both had travel rewards cards before the challenge, but they weren’t coordinating their purchases.

    Plus, they were still using debit cards for some everyday expenses.

    In short, they had room for improvement in how they made the most of the cards in their wallets.

    They started by sitting down to map out their spending habits, which uncovered three primary categories being spread across multiple cards, without any rhyme or reason:.

    Plus, they had some major wedding expenses coming up, which gave them a great opportunity to snag a fresh card with a lucrative welcome bonus.

    By coordinating their household spending, closing duplicate cards and opening a newly introduced one for the welcome offer, they’re now earning more from the same purchases they were already making.

    The remaining balance of the catering bill for their wedding alone hit the minimum spending required to earn the welcome offer, and when all was said and done, the couple took home 120,000 points — worth nearly $2,500 based on TPG’s most recent valuations.

    In a recent development, next stop for Mollie and Kevin? Southeast Asia.

    Next, we meet Amy, a single mom of two daughters in Maryland. She’s been earning rewards on her favorite hotel cobranded card for years, using it for basically every purchase she could — from utilities to groceries to clothing. She’s racked up nearly 400,000 points in the process, which have come in handy as her daughters have begun traveling for dance competitions.

    However, she was concerned her hotel loyalty meant she was sacrificing some value. Could she shift some of her spending to a latest card to diversify her rewards?

    With back-to-school shopping and dance classes making up the bulk of her spending in the next month, she opted to add a latest card to her wallet that offered solid rewards on all purchases — along with some easy-to-use statement credits.

    And a large home repair bill accelerated her progress toward earning the welcome bonus — a great way to make the best of an unexpected expense.

    Recent findings suggest that she’s still keeping her old hotel card open, since it features a low annual fee, and she’ll still want to earn (and redeem) those points when it works. However, the rewards on her new card give her the newfound flexibility she didn’t have originally.

    “I really had tunnel vision with the hotel points,” she admitted. “I was leaving money on the table.".

    Our final household focuses on Denver, a travel enthusiast who was thrown a pair of major life curveballs last year when her grandfather passed away, and her mom lost her job (and thus her source of income). She moved back home to help, and travel (understandably) shifted to the back burner.

    In a recent development, while Denver charged many purchases to her favorite travel rewards card, she had other purchases pulled straight from her bank account. She was also worried that putting everything on her credit card would encourage her to spend more. However, there was a key opportunity in her newly introduced role as a caretaker: focusing on everyday spending rather than travel rewards.

    Denver opted for a upcoming cash-back credit card with bonuses at grocery stores, on streaming services and at gas stations. It even offered a one-time $300 cash-back bonus. These rewards can immediately help offset her household bills, like medication costs, be saved for an unexpected expense, or even go toward a future getaway with her family.

    She’s continuing to pay her statement balance in full and on time, so it’s not about spending more; it’s about smarter spending based on her current situation.

    After just a month, Denver is tracking toward nearly $1,500 in cash-back rewards in the first year — just by being more intentional with her everyday spending.

    One of the most common questions we get here at TPG is, “What’s the best credit card for me?” And there’s a simple answer: “It depends.”.

    Sources indicate that everyone’s situation is unique, so there’s no one-size-fits-all approach to maximizing your everyday spending. And these three households demonstrate that exact phenomenon.

    One went with a upcoming travel card to maximize their wedding purchases. Another opted for a flexible rewards card to diversify her earnings. And the third focused on a cash-back card to support her family’s bottom line.

    All of them are now getting even more value from the purchases they were already making.

    This is the power of matching the cards in your wallet to your daily spending — while keeping a keen eye on earning the rewards that work best for you.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., mentioned he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday revealed how poisonous the politics could become.

    Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day. Democrats erupted, accusing Johnson of scaring seniors and being unwilling to fix a financial lifeline for more than 72 million retirees.

    “I think it’s outrageous,” mentioned Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., one of several Democrats on the panel who slammed Johnson for his comments. “Don’t go out there scaring Americans to make political points on Fox News. This is too fricking notable.”.

    According to recent reports, johnson acknowledged making an “imprecise comment” on prospects for a fix during the Fox interview. But he also told Democrats that if they had read his “chairman’s memo” he sent them Tuesday they would know he wants to preserve the system and pass a law to prevent any cuts to benefits if the Social Security Trust Fund is depleted.

    Industry observers note that "This is a scam, it’s grotesque, and at this point there’s really no way to fix Social Security," he noted on Fox Business. "It’s a Ponzi scheme. You can’t fix it. You just shut it down and hope you can recover some of your money.”.

    But Johnson appeared to contradict himself later in the same interview, saying there is a difference with a “government-sanctioned Ponzi scheme” in that “you can force investors to keep putting money into it and that’s what we’ll probably have to do … You can fix Social Security and make it solvent.”.

    In his opening statement at the hearing, Johnson noted Congress should pass a law to prevent benefit cuts and then “roll up our sleeves and begin seriously addressing the main problem, our massive debt and deficits.” He said that is the only way to “ensure we have the financial wherewithal to honor promises made to seniors.”.

    In a recent development, johnson also told the panel he used the term “Ponzi scheme” in part to draw attention to the importance of addressing the problem. “If I gotta pay a political price for that, I really don’t care,” he stated.

    There is no doubt that a fix is needed. Without any change, Social Security recipients face a 22 percent cut in benefits by the end of 2032, according to projections from the Social Security Board of Trustees. Johnson said Congress and the president won’t cut benefits even if the trust fund is exhausted.

    And there has been no shortage of Social Security bills introduced to provide a fix, but none of them has gained momentum.

    Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, drew flak from fellow Republicans after he and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., proposed lifting the cap on income subject to the Social Security payroll tax so that the tax would apply to all earned income.

    A bipartisan proposal, from Sens. Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., Bill Cassidy, R-La., Tim Kaine, D-Va., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, would have put a blueprint in motion by requiring the Social Security Advisory Board to recommend a bill that would ensure Social Security is funded for at least the next 50 years.

    Senators on both sides of the aisle said they were committed to fixing Social Security. Republicans stressed the importance of economic growth to bring in more revenue to the system and cautioned that tax increases would slow growth.

    Democrats pitched shifting more revenue into the system, for example by raising the cap on the payroll tax or taxing other income.

    “I do believe if we can be focused on fixing the Social Security stability issue, that could be a stepping stone to fixing broader problems,” stated Kaine, who is anticipated to chair the Budget Committee when Democrats take over Congress next year.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, JSX has acquired bankrupt New Pacific Airlines, securing a regulatory pathway to operate aircraft with more than 30 passenger seats. The airline, which abandoned its ambitious Boeing 757 operation in November 2025, was acquired in August 2026, although the deal only became public following a November 20 Department of Transportation (DOT) filing, as reported by AeroTime.

    Rather than introducing latest aircraft, JSX intends to transfer existing Embraer ERJ145-LRs into the acquired airline, increasing seating capacity from 30 to 42 passengers. The acquisition also creates opportunities beyond its immediate aims, potentially including higher-capacity turboprops, while providing greater flexibility amid ongoing regulatory scrutiny of JSX's operating model.

    Sources indicate that JSX reportedly acquired Latest Pacific for approximately $3.1 million in consideration. According to the November 20 DOT filing, the airline intends to restart operations under the JSX Air brand using two ERJ145-LRs leased from sister manufacturer Delux Public Charter, increasing to six aircraft by the fifth month. Projections include 10,106 flights and approximately 309,000 passenger boardings during the first year.

    The key acquisition is Fresh Pacific's FAA Part 121 operating certificate. JSX currently flies under Part 135, selling individual seats through the Part 380 public charter framework. This limits its aircraft to 30 passenger seats, even though its Embraer jets were originally designed to carry more. New Pacific's certificate provides a pathway to operate 42-seat aircraft, subject to regulatory approvals.

    The move also offers regulatory flexibility. AP Fresh previously reported how the FAA has proposed tightening oversight of public charter operators, following criticism from major airlines and pilot unions. Although those changes remain unresolved, a Part 121 operation could provide JSX with an alternative growth platform. Responding to questions about the acquisition, the firm told View From The Wing:.

    "JSX is continually evaluating opportunities to support its long-term growth and bring its distinctive flying experience to more customers and more communities. As part of that work, we are pursuing additional pathways that could provide even more ways to deliver our award-winning service in the future.".

    Originally known as Northern Pacific Airways, the airline planned to connect North America with Japan and South Korea through Anchorage, using Boeing 757-200 aircraft. Inspired by Icelandair's connecting-hub model, the strategy unraveled following Russian airspace restrictions in 2022. The carrier lacked the ETOPS approval required for alternative routings, forcing management to seek other markets.

    In a recent development, in July 2023, the airline instead rolled out domestic flights between Ontario, California, and Las Vegas, subsequently adding Reno and Nashville. Rebranded Fresh Pacific Airlines in September 2023, it abandoned scheduled operations in April 2024 to focus on charter flights. Management then pursued corporate and sports-team charters, converting its Boeing 757s from 181 seats to just 78 premium seats.

    US–Asia flights via Anchorage proposed.

    Russian airspace restrictions disrupt plans.

    Contract covering six NHL teams.

    Flying ends; approximately 115 employees laid off.

    Parent organization files Chapter 11.

    However, neither business model proved sustainable. According to January 2026 bankruptcy documents, the wider group burned approximately $5 million monthly during its earlier difficulties, while the NHL contract initially lost money on every flight. Expensive Boeing 757 maintenance and disputed payments worsened liquidity problems. Operations ceased in November last year, and the airline's Part 121 certificate became an crucial asset in bankruptcy proceedings.

    JSX's immediate intends involve six 42-seat ERJ145s, where it can increase capacity per aircraft by 40% over the current 30-seat layout. Paxex.aero reports that proposed routes would average 230–345 miles (370–556 km), with approximately six daily sectors per aircraft. Higher capacity could improve economics, although retaining JSX's spacious cabin, currently featuring individual seats and side tables on some aircraft, may become challenging.

    According to recent reports, the acquisition could also benefit JSX's turboprop strategy. The airline introduced ATR 42-600 flights in December 2025 with 30 premium seats per aircraft, and has outlined plans for up to 25 ATR aircraft, potentially including the larger ATR 72-600. Under Part 121, both types could theoretically accommodate substantially more passengers, provided Fresh Pacific secures the necessary aircraft-specific operating approvals.

    It has been revealed that only the 42-seat ERJ145 configuration has been unveiled. Higher-capacity ATR operations remain hypothetical.

    Ultimately, JSX could develop two complementary offerings: its established 30-seat premium service and higher-capacity flights under Part 121. Its expanding ATR operation already demonstrates a willingness to diversify aircraft types, while New Pacific's certificate offers flexibility to accommodate further growth. The acquisition therefore gives JSX more than additional seats: it provides an alternative regulatory platform without requiring the airline to abandon its existing business model.
