Up To 40,000 Extra Loyalty Points Without Spending On The Card The card awards 10,000 additional Loyalty Points at each of four thresholds during the AAdvantage qualification year, which runs March through February: Account Reaches   Cumulative Executive Card Bonuses 50,000 Loyalty Points   10,000 Loyalty Points 90,000 Loyalty Points   20,000 Loyalty Points 165,000 Loyalty Points   30,000 Loyalty Points 240,000 Loyalty Points   40,000 Loyalty Points The last two bonuses were added in the refresh. You don’t have to earn the qualifying Loyalty Points by spending on this card. Flying, shopping portal earnings, hotel bookings and spending on other AAdvantage cards can get you there. The bonuses themselves count towards subsequent thresholds. Earn 80,000 Loyalty Points outside this benefit and the first two bonuses bring you to 100,000. For someone pursuing Executive Platinum, the card can supply 30,000 of the required 200,000 Loyalty Points. Earning 170,000 elsewhere gets you there. The fourth bonus comes after Executive Platinum, helping towards higher Loyalty Point Rewards: 210,000 earned elsewhere plus the four bonuses gets you to 250,000. This is why the Executive card can make sense alongside another AAdvantage card. I have the Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees], too, and its spending can help trigger these Executive card bonuses. Globe’s Flight Streak bonuses can also stack with them. The Credits That Help Pay For The Card The October inKind addition is especially useful to me. I already use inKind at restaurants I’d eat at anyway. Here’s how the recurring credits work: $200 inKind dining credit: $100 for January–June and $100 for July–December. Add the card and benefit in the inKind app, then apply the credit when paying a participating restaurant through the app. There’s no minimum spend, and you can use it across multiple checks. Unused credit doesn’t carry over. Tips aren’t covered, and authorized users share the account’s allocation. Up to $500 American Airlines Vacations credit: Up to $250 in each half of the calendar year. This covers eligible vacation packages and Experiences purchased through American Airlines Vacations. Packages require at least two travel components, such as a flight and hotel or flight and car. Up to $100 for inflight and eligible Admirals Club purchases: A calendar year statement credit for eligible purchases charged to the card. Club food and beverages qualify. The inflight benefit applies to eligible domestic American Airlines and American Eagle flights. I won’t value this at the full $100 because many of the drinks and snacks I’d otherwise buy are already included through my status or seat, but it can cover additional purchases for family or premium club drinks. Up to $120 for Avis and Budget: Each calendar year, for eligible prepaid rentals booked directly at avis.com or budget.com and charged to the card. Pay later reservations and bookings through other travel sites don’t qualify. Up to $180 in Lyft credits: Take three eligible rides paid with the card in a calendar month, then receive a $15 Lyft credit. The credit expires after 30 days. This improved from $10 to $15 per month, but three rides are still required. Starting February 1, 2027, Wait & Save rides won’t qualify. If inKind saves you $200 on dining you’d otherwise pay for, that leaves $495 of annual fee to justify with lounge access, status bonuses and the other benefits. One old benefit is being phased out: the $10 Grubhub credit per monthly billing statement. Accounts opened before August 23, 2026 retain it through August 31, 2027. New applicants don’t get it, and the old 25% inflight food and beverage rebate has ended (replaced by the annual $100 credit). Hotel, Rental Car And Airport Benefits The refresh also added Omni Champion status and the ability to earn an annual free night. Enroll in the status benefit before your stay, allowing up to 14 days for activation. Then complete a qualifying stay of at least two consecutive nights, booked directly with Omni in your name and paid with the Executive card. That earns 100 Omni Credits for a free night on a later stay, once per calendar year. Redeem within 12 months. Taxes and resort fees are included in the award. A two-night stay you were going to make anyway can produce a valuable additional night. You can also enroll in Avis President’s Club through August 31, 2028. This offers upgrades and other rental benefits, although it’s duplicative for members who already receive it by reaching 100,000 AAdvantage Loyalty Points. Other benefits include: First checked bag free on eligible domestic American Airlines itineraries for the primary cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation. You don’t have to pay for the tickets with the card. Priority check-in, priority security where available and Group 4 boarding for the primary cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation. Up to $120 towards Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years when you pay the application fee with the card. No foreign transaction fees and travel protections including trip cancellation and interruption, trip delay, lost baggage and rental car coverage for qualifying purchases. What I’d Actually Spend On The Card The earning rates are: 12 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and AAdvantage Cars bookings. 4 miles per dollar on eligible American Airlines purchases. 1 mile per dollar on other eligible purchases. Eligible spending earns one Loyalty Point per dollar. The category bonuses don’t multiply that: a dollar of American Airlines spending earns four redeemable miles and one Loyalty Point from the card. AAdvantage Hotels can separately award miles and Loyalty Points for the booking itself. The 12-mile rate is a strong reason to use this card when booking through American’s hotel and rental car platforms. I’d also use it where payment is required to earn a credit or benefit. For everyday spending, the decision is how much the additional Loyalty Points help you. American lets card spending make a real contribution to status, but earning one redeemable mile per dollar means giving up the rewards another card would have earned. You can keep the Executive card for its clubs and milestone bonuses while putting spending on a different card. After $150,000 in purchases during a calendar year, eligible American Airlines purchases earn five miles per dollar for the rest of that year. I wouldn’t do that just to earn one additional mile per dollar on subsequent airfare.     American has nearly 50 Admirals Clubs, with more than 60 partner lounges extending the membership’s reach. Under American’s access rules:.

    Executive Platinum status by itself doesn’t get you into Admirals Clubs on ordinary domestic trips. Neither does a typical domestic first class ticket. The card also has an unusually good deal for additional cardholders: $175 total for up to three authorized customers, then $175 for each additional user. Use all three slots and that’s about $58 per person annually.

    It has been revealed that each authorized user can visit Admirals Clubs without you and bring their own eligible guests. They need their physical card, identification and an eligible same-day boarding pass. They get Admirals Club access, rather than full membership, so they don’t get the partner lounge benefit.

    For a family, $870 in total annual fees can cover a primary cardmember and three authorized users traveling separately, with guest privileges. That’s less than American charges one Executive Platinum member for standalone full membership.

    If you only want a few visits a year, the $350 annual fee Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® [See rates and fees] includes four annual Admirals Club passes.

    Industry observers note that for years American underinvested in lounges. They closed clubs, and when they renovated others the result was often the institutional look I’ve called “modern hospital.” The newer design is a huge improvement. Washington National’s E concourse club, Denver, Newark and Philadelphia show where American is going: warmer wood, better lighting, comfortable seating and spaces that feel inviting. I like this aesthetic more than the newer United Clubs or Delta Sky Clubs. The food has improved, too. I still generally prefer Delta’s lounge food, but American has moved well beyond the old snacks-and-soup proposition. Their fall Admirals Club menus include beef barbacoa taco bars in Chicago, Denver and St. Louis; sesame orange chicken at several West Coast clubs and Phoenix; and Creole style chicken with white bean cassoulet at the Newly introduced York and Newark clubs. I’ve covered American’s initiative for a new, renovated or expanded lounge nearly every month, on average, over two to three years. That’s very different from what we saw for much of the past decade. Among the projects: Charlotte: A new Admirals Club exceeding 40,000 square feet, with showers and multiple bars and food stations. Dallas–Fort Worth: A 37,000 square foot Terminal C club, plus a Provisions location planned for Terminal F. Austin: A replacement club exceeding 12,000 square feet, with American’s first outdoor lounge terrace. Chicago, Nashville, Miami and Washington National: New or expanded clubs, including Chicago’s L concourse project and the refresh of National’s Concourse D club. There’s also the Provisions grab-and-go concept, already operating in Charlotte, with additional locations announced for New York JFK and Dallas–Fort Worth. Sometimes you want food to take to the gate more than you want a seat in a lounge. And the most valuable part of a club can still be its agents. I’ve written about the Austin agents who keep looking for better connections after I’ve left. Having someone help fix a disrupted trip can be worth more than everything you eat and drink in the lounge that year. The Initial Bonus And Who Can Get It The current public initial bonus is 80,000 AAdvantage miles after $8,000 in purchases within the first three months of account opening. The annual fee is $695. Those are redeemable miles. The initial bonus doesn’t count as Loyalty Points towards status, although eligible spending to earn it does. Under Citi’s terms, you aren’t eligible for the initial bonus if you’ve received an Executive card new account bonus within the past 48 months. The restriction also covers converting another Citi card into an Executive account when that other account earned a new account bonus within the last 48 months. Simply having a different AAdvantage cobrand card doesn’t disqualify you. Then complete a qualifying stay of at least two consecutive nights, booked directly with Omni in your name and paid with the Executive card. A two-night stay you were going to make anyway can produce a valuable additional night. You can also enroll in Avis President’s Club through August 31, 2028. This offers upgrades and other rental benefits, although it’s duplicative for members who already receive it by reaching 100,000 AAdvantage Loyalty Points. Other benefits include: First checked bag free on eligible domestic American Airlines itineraries for the primary cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation. You don’t have to pay for the tickets with the card. Priority check-in, priority security where available and Group 4 boarding for the primary cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation. Up to $120 towards Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years when you pay the application fee with the card. No foreign transaction fees and travel protections including trip cancellation and interruption, trip delay, lost baggage and rental car coverage for qualifying purchases. What I’d Actually Spend On The Card The earning rates are: 12 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and AAdvantage Cars bookings. 4 miles per dollar on eligible American Airlines purchases. 1 mile per dollar on other eligible purchases. Eligible spending earns one Loyalty Point per dollar. The category bonuses don’t multiply that: a dollar of American Airlines spending earns four redeemable miles and one Loyalty Point from the card. AAdvantage Hotels can separately award miles and Loyalty Points for the booking itself. The 12-mile rate is a strong reason to use this card when booking through American’s hotel and rental car platforms. I’d also use it where payment is required to earn a credit or benefit. American lets card spending make a real contribution to status, but earning one redeemable mile per dollar means giving up the rewards another card would have earned. You can keep the Executive card for its clubs and milestone bonuses while putting spending on a different card. After $150,000 in purchases during a calendar year, eligible American Airlines purchases earn five miles per dollar for the rest of that year.     #100200. Breaking: Spirit Airlines Shut Down—Did It Forget To Cancel Its Internet? Comcast Wants $1.25 Million

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1161 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Spirit Airlines Shut Down—Did It Forget To Cancel Its Internet? Comcast Wants $1.25 Million

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1161 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Spirit Airlines stopped flying in May, but Comcast and its subsidiaries say it still owes $1.25 million in internet bills.
    • Part of this sounds like Spirit forgot to turn off its internet when it moved out.
    • Their November 19 court filing asks the bankruptcy judge to order payment and make Spirit decide whether to keep or reject the contracts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Spirit Airlines stopped flying in May, but Comcast and its subsidiaries say it still owes $1.25 million in internet bills. Some charges are for locations Spirit says it left in 2024—but the providers say they haven’t produced records showing the service was canceled. Always keep proof when dealing with Comcast! Part of this sounds like Spirit forgot to turn off its internet when it moved out. According to the providers, on October 22 the airline authorized them to disconnect every location except Dania Pointe in Dania Beach, Florida. That was nearly six months after the airline stopped flying. Their November 19 court filing asks the bankruptcy judge to order payment and make Spirit decide whether to keep or reject the contracts. Comcast and its Masergy subsidiary say some services were still running when they filed. Spirit shut down on May 2 after it couldn’t obtain the money to keep operating. No one would continue to fund its massive losses. But the bankruptcy process to unwind its business remains ongoing. There are assets to sell, contracts to resolve, records to maintain and creditors arguing over who gets paid. I’ve covered the lawsuit from workers seeking 60 days of pay over the abrupt shutdown and the court-approved $668 million sale of a 27-aircraft portfolio. Much of that aircraft price represented lenders applying what Spirit owed them toward their purchase. The four internet providers list these unpaid balances: Provider Amount Claimed Comcast Cable Communications Management $219,743.41 Masergy Cloud Communications $164,626.99 Masergy Communications $849,646.45 Nitel $11,990.73 Total $1,246,007.58 Comcast acquired Masergy in 2021 and Nitel in 2025. This is for internet service at Spirit locations, not inflight wifi (which was provided by Thales). The providers say they’ve repeatedly sought payment. Spirit responded that some locations had been vacated in 2024, and that disconnection requests should have been submitted for others. You might expect the internet companies simply to get in line with Spirit’s other unpaid creditors. For bills dating to before the bankruptcy, that’s probably what happens. But these companies say they continued providing services after Spirit filed on August 29, 2025. Necessary expenses of running a tech giant in bankruptcy can qualify as administrative expenses, which get priority over other unsecured debts, or else no one would keep supplying a bankrupt business trying to turn itself around. And services needed to sell its assets and administer the remaining business can continue to qualify. It’s unclear what treatment will apply to internet Spirit was no longer using, even if it hadn’t cancelled the contracts. Comcast needs to establish the benefit their services supplied to the bankruptcy estate. In fact, their motion cites In re Enron but that denied administrative priority for unused pipeline capacity that hadn’t benefited the estate. Internet connections supporting the Spirit Airlines liquidation are likely to get repayment priority But defunct services that hadn’t merely been cancelled might not. A hearing is scheduled for December 16, with responses due December 9. And even a successful priority claim doesn’t necessarily mean Comcast gets immediate payment. In Midway Airlines, a telephone equipment lessor won an administrative claim for unpaid lease obligations, but the appeals court upheld making it wait for payment alongside other administrative creditors. So Comcast may have to wait as long for payment as you wait on hold to schedule a service appointment. Topics on this pageBankruptcyComcastSpirit AirlinesFlorida+1 more More From View from the Wing.

    #100199. Tech Report: The Real Stakes of the Wilderness Years

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (201 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nationalreview ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: The Real Stakes of the Wilderness Years

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (201 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that as we get closer to final results from the 2026 midterms, the scale of the carnage comes more clearly into view.
    • In the Senate, Democrats gained nine seats, the biggest swing since Republicans’ nine-seat pickup in 2014.
    • Dan McLaughlin is a senior writer at National Review Online and a fellow at National Review Institute.

    Industry observers note that as we get closer to final results from the 2026 midterms, the scale of the carnage comes more clearly into view. The question is not whether Republicans can recover from this, but whether the American system of government will be changed irreparably before they do. To what will Republicans return?

    In the Senate, Democrats gained nine seats, the biggest swing since Republicans’ nine-seat pickup in 2014. With 56 senators, it’s the Democrats’ biggest majority since 2009–10, when they peaked at 60 seats. Republicans haven’t had that many Senate seats since 1922, when the caucus was 59 seats after the 1920 landslide that repudiated Woodrow Wilson’s progressivism and swept Warren Harding into office. If you’re wondering, the largest-ever Republican Senate caucus, in absolute numbers rather than as a share of the chamber, was 60 in 1907; the largest Democratic caucus was 75 seats at the peak of the New Deal in 1937. There’s a reason why Franklin D. Roosevelt thought he could get away with Court-packing with 75 senators.

    Dan McLaughlin is a senior writer at National Review Online and a fellow at National Review Institute.

    On “The Real Stakes of the Wilderness Years”.

    #100197. At the Races: The new Trump Democrats

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1932 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    At the Races: The new Trump Democrats

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1932 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Editor’s note: At the Races will not publish next week on Thanksgiving Day.
    • By Niels Lesniewski, Mary Ellen McIntire and Daniela Altimari.
    • Senate Democrats powered their way to a majority by flipping nine seats – their biggest gain in nearly 70 years.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Editor’s note: At the Races will not publish next week on Thanksgiving Day. We’ll be back the following week.

    By Niels Lesniewski, Mary Ellen McIntire and Daniela Altimari.

    Senate Democrats powered their way to a majority by flipping nine seats – their biggest gain in nearly 70 years.

    Eight of those wins were in states that Donald Trump has carried every time he’s run so it’s no surprise that some of the incoming senators are talking up the prospect of working with him over the next two years.

    “We don't have time to wait until we have a different administration in the White House,” South Carolina Sen.-elect Annie Andrews told reporters this week. “We have two years ahead of us. We have very real problems that we need to address.”.

    Industry observers note that andrews is the first Democrat elected to the Senate from South Carolina since 1998. A pediatrician, she cited reducing prescription drug costs as a potential area of common ground with Trump.

    In a recent development, “I support the president's attempts to stop taxes on tips and taxes on Social Security,” Andrews said, citing two selling points of last year’s GOP reconciliation law. During the campaign, she issued a policy paper expressing support for making those provisions of the tax code permanent.

    James Talarico, the incoming senator from Texas, told fellow Democrats gathered in Denver last week that if Trump wanted “the same plaques and portraits and busts as LBJ, we can help make that a reality.”.

    “We should make the final two years of his presidency the most productive of any presidency in American history,” noted Talarico, the first Democrat in nearly 40 years to win a Senate race in the Lone Star State.

    The idea of Trump and congressional Democrats working together might seem far-fetched, but with the incoming Democrats hailing from places such as Alaska, the Carolinas, Mississippi, Kansas and Texas, there’s a political incentive to appeal to Republican-leaning voters back home.

    But intentionally or not, Talarico and other newly elected Democrats might be borrowing from the playbook of Upcoming York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who has welcomed Trump when goals align, including on an effort to redevelop the Sunnyside rail yard in the president’s native Queens.

    Trump has stressed that he will veto legislation he opposes from the incoming Democratic Congress, but, at least for the moment, he seems open to deals.

    “I have a feeling that this is going to be an unbelievably productive two years,” Trump told Fox News early Thursday morning in Shenzhen, China, adding that  he would invite Democrats to the White House.

    According to recent reports, “I respect them,” he said. “Politics is a nasty game, and they won.”.

    Peltola prevails: Former Rep. Mary Peltola’s victory over Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska brings the Senate Democratic Caucus to 56 seats in the 120th Congress. Peltola finished with just over 50 percent of the vote, negating the need to use the state’s ranked choice voting system. The race for the state’s at-large House district was decided by a ranked choice tally, with Republican Rep. Nick Begich defeating independent Bill Hill 51 percent to 49 percent in the final round. Alaska voters also rejected an attempt to eliminate ranked choice voting in the state by a vote of 54 percent to 46 percent.

    Leadership elections: House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries to serve as the next speaker in a 251-11 closed-door Wednesday vote, Roll Call’s Lauren Green reports. That puts Jeffries in prime position to become the first Black speaker when the full chamber votes in January. Meanwhile, Senate Democrats are scheduled to pick the next majority leader on Dec. 1, as our colleague Savannah Behrmann reports. Charles E. Schumer, who’s being challenged by Maryland’s Chris Van Hollen, maintains he has the votes to win.

    A victory lap and a warning: Even as the Congressional Hispanic Caucus celebrates its largest roster ever, the group’s leaders had a warning for their fellow Democrats: “Latino voters gave Democrats a two-year lease, but it expires in 2028 unless the party changes its playbook for good,” stated California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez, who leads the group’s campaign arm.

    #KYGOV: Republican Rep. James R. Comer, who was just elected to a sixth full term, launched his much-anticipated run for Kentucky governor this week. The Bluegrass State is one of three states holding statewide executive  elections in 2027, along with Louisiana and Mississippi.

    Rocky Mountain roundup: Rep. Lauren Boebert, an outspoken Republican with a national reputation as a Second Amendment provocateur, lost her bid for reelection in Colorado’s 4th District to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired Navy rear admiral. Meanwhile, Republican Gabe Evans, who fell short in his bid for a second term in the neighboring 8th District, announced he looks to challenge Laubacher in two years, Roll Call’s Samantha Freeman reports.

    They’re back: Our colleague Nina Heller tracked down former congressional staffers who are back on the Hill as newly elected members. “I never thought this would be the path, but I’m honored to do it,” said Rep.-elect Sydney Gruters, who worked for fellow Florida Republicans Greg Steube and Vern Buchanan, her soon-to-be House predecessor.

    RIP: Former Rep. Jim McDermott, a longtime advocate for universal health care, died last week at the age of 89. The Washington Democrat, who retired to a small town in southwestern France after 28 years in the House, was hailed by his home state’s senior senator, Patty Murray, “as one of the first and most powerful voices fighting to fix our broken health care system in Congress.”.

    Where the House stands: As of 3 p.m. Eastern time, House Democrats have flipped 46 seats to three for the Republicans and are on track to hold at least 257 seats in the next Congress. Six races remain uncalled by The Associated Press, including two in Louisiana that will be decided by December runoffs. The AP is also yet to call Tennessee’s 4th District, where Republican Rep. Scott DesJarlais has conceded to Democrat Victoria Broderick, who leads by 272 votes out of nearly 200,000 cast.

    Thompson loses: California Rep. Mike Thompson lost his bid for a 15th term to former venture capitalist Eric Jones, a political newcomer who poured millions into his campaign. Thompson is the second California member to lose to a fellow Democrat this year, after Rep. Jimmy Gomez. But Rep. Doris Matsui held off an intraparty challenge from democratic socialist Mai Vang.

    2028 draft: Supporters of former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg introduced Team Pete PAC on Thursday, an effort to urge him to launch a second presidential bid.

    Battleground rep: Michigan Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet will be House Democrats' battleground leadership representative in the next Congress, acting as a bridge between members in competitive districts and party leadership. McDonald Rivet, who ran unopposed for the position, will succeed Nevada Rep. Susie Lee.

    #INGOV: Indiana Gov. Mike Braun rolled out his 2028 reelection campaign as speculation swirls that state Attorney General Todd Rokita could challenge him for the Republican nomination. Rokita, a former congressman, has criticized Braun for not disciplining state educators who posted controversial comments after Charlie Kirk’s assassination but said last week that he wanted Braun to “run for governor” and “be successful.” The two previously faced off in a 2018 Republican Senate primary, with Braun going on to serve one term in the Senate.

    Latest leader for New Dems: Illinois Rep. Nikki Budzinski will chair the New Democrat Coalition next year, taking over from fellow Illinois Rep. Brad Schneider. New Mexico’s Gabe Vasquez, Ohio’s Greg Landsman and Washington’s Kim Schrier and Marilyn Strickland will serve as co-chairs of the center-left group, the largest ideological entity in the Democratic Caucus.

    According to recent reports, remembering Holden: Former Pennsylvania Rep. Tim Holden, who served 10 terms in the House before losing a Democratic primary to Matt Cartwright in 2012, died Sunday at the age of 69. House members held a moment of silence for Holden on the floor Thursday. Republican Rep. Dan Meuser, whose district includes territory Holden once represented, described him as “well-liked and widely respected, including by those on both sides of the political aisle.”.

    Investigated: Ohio Rep.-elect Brian Poindexter is under investigation for alleged sexual harassment after the Democrat’s campaign hired a human resources firm to investigate the complaint. Both the Blue Dog PAC and the Congressional Progressive Caucus, which had endorsed Poindexter’s candidacy, dropped their support in the closing days of the campaign after learning of the allegation.

    Recent findings suggest that tennessee two-step: Tennessee Democrat Jeri Green, who narrowly lost the open governor’s race to Republican Sen. Marsha Blackburn, revealed a bid for the state Senate seat GOP Rep.-elect Brent Taylor is expected to vacate. Taylor narrowly defeated Democratic state Rep. Justin Pearson in the redrawn 9th District, though both men were simultaneously reelected to their legislative seats.

    Industry observers note that the  historic “blue tsunami” that swept Democrats into commanding Senate and House majorities has some pundits questioning whether Republicans will ever be in charge again, observes Roll Call elections analyst Nathan L. Gonzales of Inside Elections.

    But you just have to look at the election results from two years ago to realize that when it comes to winning party coalitions, nothing is permanent anymore, Nathan writes.

    Only the young: Upcoming York magazine catches up with young Republicans in South Carolina and finds that immigration policy and the war in Iran have turned many of the MAGA faithful against the GOP.

    From satirist to senator: The Washington Post traces South Carolina Democrat Annie Andrews’ journey from an online agitator who made relentless fun of Republicans to a newly elected senator who claims she’s eager to work with her GOP colleagues.

    Bad blood: The Boston Globe explores the long-standing rivalry between Maine’s two newest members of Congress: Democratic Sen.-elect Troy Jackson and Republican Rep.-elect Paul LePage.

    Schumer’s choice: Uncertainty around whether Schumer will seek another term in 2028 has risen as the Latest York Democrat seeks to become Senate majority leader next year, Politico reports.

    That's how long it's been since the Senate Democratic Caucus last saw a contested race for its top leadership position, with Maryland’s Van Hollen now challenging Schumer for the job.

    After Democrats lost eight Senate seats (and their majority) in the 1994 Republican Revolution, 42-year old South Dakota Sen. Tom Daschle edged out Connecticut's Christopher J. Dodd by a single vote, 24-23, to succeed outgoing leader George Mitchell of Maine.

    The last time a sitting Democratic Senate leader faced a formal challenge was a decade earlier, in 1984.

    It has been revealed that west Virginia's Robert C. Byrd, who’d been leading his party in the chamber since 1977, easily fended off a bid by Florida’s Lawton Chiles.

    According to recent reports, the last time either party experienced a contested race for the position was four years ago, when Florida Sen. Rick Scott challenged Republican leader Mitch McConnell of Kentucky.

    As Byrd did before him, McConnell handily defeated his challenger in the secret-ballot vote.

    Industry observers note that machine recounts in a pair of House races in North Carolina are expected to be completed Monday. Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx trails Democrat Chuck Hubbard by 331 votes, while GOP Rep. Pat Harrigan leads Democratic challenger Ashley Bell by just over 2,500 votes. The trailing candidate could then request a partial hand recount.

    Monday is also the deadline for Republican Rep. Brad Finstad to formally request a recount in his razor-thin race against Democrat Jake Johnson in Minnesota’s 1st District. Finstad, who reportedly remarked he’ll seek one, trails Johnson by 321 votes.

    Hilton Diamond Guest Claims He Gets Sent Next Door For Coffee—And Treated Like He Was Stealing Breakfast

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2400 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that I’ve written about people walking into hotels where they aren’t staying and helping themselves to a full breakfast.
    • John Konrad’s account of the coffee dispute, November 21, 2026.
    • Recent findings suggest that in the second half of the thread, the manager talks up Homewood’s overnight oats.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that I’ve written about people walking into hotels where they aren’t staying and helping themselves to a full breakfast. Somehow getting an actual guest a cup of coffee can be more complicated.

    John Konrad’s account of the coffee dispute, November 21, 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that in the second half of the thread, the manager talks up Homewood’s overnight oats. Konrad decides he’d like some after all. He’s refused because he’s registered next door. He raises his voice, objects to being told to calm down (no one in history has ever calmed down because they’ve been told to calm down), and eventually refuses an offered gym pass.

    I AM A DIAMOND MEMBER BEING CROSS-EXAMINED OVER CHIA SEEDS.

    The replies include plenty of people who think he’s being insufferable. One person who notes they’ve stayed at both properties reports that guests routinely move between them. When a critic calls him a Karen, Konrad points back to his Curb Your Enthusiasm framing making himself part of the joke.

    It has been revealed that the two hotels have shared ownership by the Mian Companies. Signs direct Hilton Garden Inn guests to Homewood’s gym during construction. Homewood Suites Oxnard/Camarillo includes breakfast for its guests. Hilton Garden Inn has a different model. In the United States, eligible Gold and Diamond members who select the benefit receive a $10 daily food and beverage credit per person, for up to two registered guests. And asking for a room number when someone complains about a key is normal. A hotel employee can help with access. But a staff referral should make getting coffee easy. If the two hotels haven’t agreed on what guests can use, they need to sort that out between themselves. Meanwhile, People Really Do Walk Into Hotels For Free Breakfast I’ve covered people walking into a Drury Inn just to eat and people stopping at hotels for breakfast on their way to work. At many limited service properties, nobody checks. Looking comfortable in the lobby can be enough. At the aloft Dallas Love Field in 2022, I selected breakfast as my Marriott elite welcome amenity instead of 500 points. The Aloft and Element occupied the same building, with separate entrances. Breakfast meant walking over to the Element’s lobby buffet, which was included for guests staying there. Nobody asked my name, room number, or whether I’d selected breakfast. I could have taken the points and eaten anyway. Someone who wasn’t staying at either hotel could have walked in just as easily. This favors people who look like they belong. Konrad adds that he hadn’t shaved and his clothes were stained from boat work. He thinks that may explain some of the suspicion. There are real costs to feeding people who aren’t guests. There are also costs to policing breakfast: staff time, lines, and embarrassing the customers who are supposed to be there. A hotel can spend more trying to prevent a small loss than the food would have cost, especially if it chases away repeat business. Hotels Keep Getting Coffee Wrong I’ve been writing about the importance of hotel coffee for years. A business hotel ought to have drinkable coffee available around the clock, with real milk or cream. Guests arrive from other time zones, wake up early for flights, and get up before dawn to work. Their day have to start when the restaurant opens. At what was then the W San Diego, I was staying in the Extreme Wow suite. Still on East Coast time, I woke around 4:30 a.m. At about 5 I called the Whatever/Whenever line for coffee. They told me it wasn’t available until 6. They couldn’t provide whatever (coffee) whenever (in the morning). I wound up walking to Starbucks. I’ve also written about: The then-Andaz Wall Street removing its 24 hour lobby coffee, when rooms didn’t have coffee machines and room service wasn’t available around the clock. Hyatt Herald Square’s coffee stand opening 30 minutes late. Park Hyatt Washington offering 24 hour room service, but refusing overnight coffee. There was a Starbucks across the street there, too. And I don’t love Starbucks, they’re simply ubiquitous. And then there’s the time the Sheraton Macao investigated me for trying to steal coffee. I ordered six cups from room service. After pouring two, the pot was nearly empty. I called down, and they agreed to send four more. Instead, at 6:30 a.m. the delivery employee appeared at my door and announced: I am here to investigate. He insisted the machine was electronic, so it couldn’t have dispensed too little. Then he poured out what remained. Half a cup. There I was in my bathrobe, establishing that six cups and two and a half cups weren’t the same thing before he’d hand over the replacement coffee he’d already brought upstairs. Starwood apologized and offered 5,000 Starpoints. I declined. The hotel’s in-room dining manager apologized as well. They’d turned a short pot of coffee into a staff investigation, a corporate response, and an offer of points. Bringing the coffee would have been cheaper.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that ES Foundry, a U.S.
    • According to the tech giant, it is the first and only crystalline silicon solar cell manufacturer to ship more than 1 gigawatt (GW) of domestically manufactured solar cells in the United States.
    • solar cell manufacturers with a fully operational facility producing and shipping cells to customers, ES Foundry is helping move American solar manufacturing to commercial reality.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that ES Foundry, a U.S. manufacturer of high-efficiency solar cells, is at RE+ 2026 this week to showcase its American-made solar cells and announce a milestone in its operating capacity.

    According to the tech giant, it is the first and only crystalline silicon solar cell manufacturer to ship more than 1 gigawatt (GW) of domestically manufactured solar cells in the United States.

    As one of the few U.S. solar cell manufacturers with a fully operational facility producing and shipping cells to customers, ES Foundry is helping move American solar manufacturing to commercial reality.

    Recent findings suggest that in July, the company unveiled it reached its full 3-GW manufacturing capacity. The company began production on its first 1-GW line last year and has now completed its 2-GW expansion line.

    Solar Power World attended the opening of its Greenwood, South Carolina facility last year, reporting on its manufacturing outfit and its unique approach to supply deals that include working with large-scale project developers and utilities to guarantee domestic content supplies.

    Industry observers note that at RE+, attendees can see its U.S.-manufactured high-efficiency monocrystalline bifacial PERC solar cells and meet with company representatives to discuss domestic sourcing, manufacturing capabilities, and the evolving needs of the U.S. solar market.

    “There’s an key difference between talking about building a domestic solar supply chain and actually making it happen,” said ES Foundry CEO Alex Zhu in a statement. “At ES Foundry, we’re manufacturing at commercial scale, shipping cells to customers and navigating the realities of U.S. production every day. That experience gives us a unique perspective on what it will take to build a competitive, sustainable American solar industry. Success requires more than manufacturing capacity. It requires the right economics, technology investments, customer demand and policies to support long-term growth. We’re proud to be delivering on the promise of American manufacturing today while helping shape the industry’s future.”.

    Visit ES Foundry at RE+ 2026: Booth C7434, November 16–19, Las Vegas, Nevada.

    #100193. Caring for Aging Loved Ones Is Not an Injustice

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (192 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nationalreview ↗ Open Full Page

    Caring for Aging Loved Ones Is Not an Injustice

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (192 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Saturday Night Live struck a nerve with its recent “Sister” skit, a spoof advertisement for a supposedly revolutionary elder-care service that is free, available around the clock, and conveniently happens to be your sister.
    • In a recent development, there’s certainly some truth to this, but there’s a difference between objecting to an unfair division of caregiving responsibilities and treating those responsibilities as inherently oppressive.
    • Heather Madden is the vice president for policy initiatives at Independent Women.

    Saturday Night Live struck a nerve with its recent “Sister” skit, a spoof advertisement for a supposedly revolutionary elder-care service that is free, available around the clock, and conveniently happens to be your sister. The skit is funny because it captures something many families recognize: When an aging parent needs help, it’s often the women who step up, while male relatives carry on with their lives largely uninterrupted.

    In a recent development, there’s certainly some truth to this, but there’s a difference between objecting to an unfair division of caregiving responsibilities and treating those responsibilities as inherently oppressive. The suggestion that our elder-care challenges are largely a product of sexism, or that women who take on these responsibilities have simply been conditioned to accept their own exploitation, misses the bigger problem. This interpretation not only diminishes the contributions of female caregivers but also feeds into a troubling cultural narrative: that caring for the people we love is an injustice rather than a responsibility inherent to family.

    Heather Madden is the vice president for policy initiatives at Independent Women.

    On “Caring for Aging Loved Ones Is Not an Injustice”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that american Airlines is dropping its lawsuit over Chicago O’Hare’s gate redistribution.
    • The airline has recovered gate space, added flights, and is in a much stronger position in Chicago than when the case began.
    • American says two subsequent gate redeterminations have increased its allocation, and it also bought two gates from Spirit Airlines.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that american Airlines is dropping its lawsuit over Chicago O’Hare’s gate redistribution. The airline tells me it has filed to dismiss the underlying contract case after losing its injunction appeal — even as it continues to insist Chicago broke its lease. The airline has recovered gate space, added flights, and is in a much stronger position in Chicago than when the case began. American says two subsequent gate redeterminations have increased its allocation, and it also bought two gates from Spirit Airlines. They’re putting their attention into growing the hub, including a upcoming Admirals Club that doubles the current L concourse lounge’s footprint. In a statement shared with me, American says: We stand by our decision to advocate for a fair process, and today, we believe the best way to continue delivering on that commitment is to look ahead. As rebuild our Chicago hub from the pandemic, we have continued to invest in our operation, network and customer experience. Our focus now is on continuing that momentum and building an even stronger future at O’Hare. American’s filing goes further – it asks to dismiss the entire lawsuit with prejudice, including its claim for money damages. Chicago and United don’t object, and each side would bear its own costs and legal fees. Once approved, that closes the door on American returning to collect damages over the same 2025 gate redistribution. American Is Choosing To Drop The Case Earlier today I explained that losing the appeal didn’t end American’s lawsuit. The appeals court upheld the denial of a preliminary injunction because it accepted that undoing the gate changes would cause greater disruption than leaving them in place. It didn’t finally decide whether Chicago breached the 2018 lease, or whether doing so damaged American. The airline is now choosing to stop pursuing that underlying case. The airline maintains that the 2025 process violated its agreement and gave United an unfair head start, but says the changed circumstances at O’Hare make investing and competing there a better focus. I still think American has the better contract argument. The city promised additional gate capacity and a protected period to grow into it before another redistribution. The trial judge accepted that the promise had been made, but suggested that even if Chicago was breaking that promise it might not be enforceable. But the evidence in the case was pretty clear that Chicago was redistributing gates earlier than they’d promised to, and that the timing was part of American’s bargained-for consideration in signing the lease. I was skeptical from the beginning that American would get an injunction, because its losses seemed potentially compensable with money. But I also suggested that American had recovered its gate position so the value in litigation seemed almost beside the point at this point. More Flights, More Destinations, And Gates Coming Back Before American sued, it planned forup to 480 daily departures and a network of about 150 destinations. Summer 2025 represented 22% more departures and 25% more seats than the prior year. American now has more than 500 daily departures and service to more than 185 destinations in 20 countries and territories. Chicago is its third-largest hub, with nearly 10,000 employees. And their spring 2026 schedule called for more than 500 peak daily departures, with 30% more departures than spring 2025. American counts more than 30 new destinations added or declared from Chicago since the start of 2025. Naples released in May 2025 and Honolulu that October. Maui starts December 17, while Tokyo Narita starts March 19, 2027. This growth earned back gate space in this October’s redistribution. Separately, it paid $30 million for Spirit’s G8 and G10 gate leases, which I was first to report. A Bigger Admirals Club And Better Facilities The new L concourse Admirals Club will replace American’s smallest and weakest O’Hare lounge next year. The current space is basically a sad room with a bar and a small conference room. It’s convenient to the L gates, but it isn’t much of a reason to choose American. The replacement will exceed 10,000 square feet and double the current footprint, with floor-to-ceiling windows, airfield views, and the newer design American has introduced in places like Washington National, Denver, Newark, and Philadelphia. The existing club remains open during construction. American’s rendering shows what they’re building: Refurbished gates K1 and L2A have reopened with larger waiting areas, and baggage claim carousels 30 through 33 are operating. American has also invested in the product passengers get once they board: Its O’Hare operation now offers a premium cabin on every flight, after replacing single class regional jets with aircraft offering first class and Wi-Fi. Chicago received the new Boeing 787-9s with 51 business class suites first. United Still Has To Compete With American In Chicago United wanted American to back away from O’Hare. Scott Kirby talked up American’s losses and tried to get financial analysts to pressure the airline to retreat. United filed more flying to keep American from improving its gate position, even though it didn’t independently want all of that additional capacity. The Federal Aviation Administration concluded that the airport couldn’t handle the schedules airlines had filed. Its summer flight caps used approved 2025 schedules as the baseline, rather than rewarding United for its much bigger proposed buildup. That protected American’s competitive position. The federal intervention and American’s recovered gate space have mattered more to its ability to stay and grow than the injunction appeal. American still has to make the flying work. But Kirby’s preferred answer—have American leave so United can dominate—would also cost American connecting traffic, local customers, and credit card spending. The airline tells me it’s seeing growth in local and business customers, AAdvantage enrollments, and credit card acquisitions. It’s also bringing in Margaret Mueller, former head of the Executives’ Club of Chicago, as vice president and managing partner for the market starting November 30. Her job includes local sales and business relationships. That’s where the larger schedule and lounge spending have to pay off. Chicago is one of the biggest credit card spending markets in the country. American needs a schedule customers can use and an experience they’ll choose if it wants them earning AAdvantage miles on their everyday spending. The new Admirals Club also gives them a more tangible reason to keep paying for the Citi AAdvantage Executive card.     #100191. Delta Holding December 2 Seattle Event To Announce Fresh Singapore Flight—And Pick A Fight With Its Former Partner

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3207 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Delta Holding December 2 Seattle Event To Announce Fresh Singapore Flight—And Pick A Fight With Its Former Partner

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3207 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Delta Air Lines is throwing an Asian night market in Seattle on December 2, where they’ll finally reveal non-stop Singapore service.
    • Recent findings suggest that enilria reported the December 2 Seattle announcement several days ago and highlighted the invitation’s Asian theme.
    • Heard the Delta Seattle event has an Asian destination inspired holiday night market theme.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Delta Air Lines is throwing an Asian night market in Seattle on December 2, where they’ll finally reveal non-stop Singapore service. That would put Delta into a roughly 17 hour nonstop fight with Singapore Airlines, giving its customers a way to reach one of Asia’s most vital business centers without changing planes in Seoul. Enilria reported the December 2 Seattle announcement several days ago and highlighted the invitation’s Asian theme. Aviation watchdog JonNYC has now corroborated that direction, reporting that the event has an “Asian destination inspired holiday night market theme,” then adding: “Singapore as in.” Heard the Delta Seattle event has an Asian destination inspired holiday night market theme — JonNYC (@xJonNYC) November 23, 2026 The invitation is for Delta Night Market at MOPOP, Seattle’s Museum of Pop Culture, on Wednesday, December 2 from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. It promises food, drinks, shopping and cultural experiences built around Asian destinations, along with city-inspired charms guests can collect. The line that caught Enilria’s attention: Seven destinations. One unforgettable night. Delta’s current and unveiled East and Southeast Asian destinations are Tokyo, Seoul, Shanghai, Taipei, Hong Kong and Manila. That’s seven airports when you count both Tokyo Haneda and Narita, but six cities. If they’re counting cities, Singapore makes seven. So I don’t take this to mean seven latest routes, though of course there may be additional routes announced. . And there’s a more concrete clue than the party theme. In a July 29 presentation to a Pacific air traffic coordination group, Delta wrote: New markets announced for 2027 are Manila and Singapore. This Has Been Coming For More Than A Year I reported Delta’s prepares to return to Singapore and Manila in October 2025. The following month, I wrote about their internal view that Europe was already pretty full, and that future long haul growth would lean heavily toward Asia, from both Los Angeles and Seattle. JonNYC has been all over this story. In August, Delta revealed at an event for its largest corporate customers that Singapore would follow closely behind Manila. Los Angeles–Manila is scheduled to begin March 28, 2027, initially three times weekly before going daily June 7. Delta last served Singapore in September 2019, as a flight from Tokyo Narita. They dismantled the connecting hub inherited from Northwest, moved their U.S.–Tokyo flying to Haneda and relied more heavily on Korean Air’s Seoul hub to get passengers elsewhere in Asia. Singapore Is A Market Delta Needs To Sell Singapore combines regional headquarters, finance, technology and a wealthy local market. For the multinational business traffic Delta wants, it has become more important than Hong Kong. There are now several times as many regional corporate headquarters in Singapore than Hong Kong.     General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    House Ethics panel adopts changes aimed at speeding up investigations

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (654 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ethics Chairman Michael Guest, left, and ranking member Mark DeSaulnier arrive for a committee meeting on Capitol Hill in April.
    • In a year roiled by sexual misconduct allegations in the House, the Ethics Committee approved a series of changes Thursday that its members say are intended to improve how the panel handles its investigations.
    • In a rare public meeting lasting less than 10 minutes, the committee discussed proposed tweaks aimed at speeding up its processes, after some observers have criticized its pace.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ethics Chairman Michael Guest, left, and ranking member Mark DeSaulnier arrive for a committee meeting on Capitol Hill in April. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    In a year roiled by sexual misconduct allegations in the House, the Ethics Committee approved a series of changes Thursday that its members say are intended to improve how the panel handles its investigations.

    In a rare public meeting lasting less than 10 minutes, the committee discussed proposed tweaks aimed at speeding up its processes, after some observers have criticized its pace.

    “My problem with the Ethics Committee is it just takes too damn long,” Rep. Madeleine Dean, D-Pa., said earlier this year.

    The internal rule changes were adopted in a voice vote by the committee, which is evenly divided between Republicans and Democrats.

    “We believe that these rule changes will provide more transparency. They will expedite our investigative process while maintaining protections for witnesses and victims, while also making sure that … due process is protected,” Chair Michael Guest, R-Miss., said during the meeting.

    When former Reps. Eric Swalwell, D-Calif., and Tony Gonzales, R-Texas, resigned earlier this year amid misconduct allegations, it sparked outrage as some called to rethink how the House polices bad behavior. Both men were on the radar of the Ethics Committee at the time, but such investigations have tended to move slowly.

    “I want the Ethics Committee to move faster,” stated panel member Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., back in April.

    Industry observers note that the committee did not immediately make available the exact text of the changes it adopted Thursday. But a summary sent in a news release earlier this week included one proposal aimed at “consolidating deadlines” for a member to respond to an investigative subcommittee’s findings. Another tweak aimed at speeding things up would give the chair and ranking member subpoena power on behalf of the committee, rather than requiring a full committee vote.

    The summary described “codifying the Committee’s policy of publicly disclosing any findings that a Member engaged in sexual harassment or other sexual misconduct” while “prohibiting publication of the identity of any victim.”.

    Also on the list: “Expanding the circumstances under which fines and denials of privileges are considered an appropriate sanction to include any abuses of position.”.

    According to recent reports, it comes as women on both sides of the aisle have formed a partnership aimed at reviewing how Congress deals with sexual misconduct and suggesting concrete ideas for an overhaul. Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, D-N.M., has been co-leading that effort as the chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus alongside Republican Women’s Caucus head Kat Cammack, R-Fla.

    According to Leger Fernández, the Ethics Committee has “consulted” with her group as it weighed the changes to its internal rules.

    “The Ethics Committee was clearly listening to women staffers, and has been a great partner in our work. We appreciate how they’ve consulted DWC and that these proposals will improve transparency and help protect the identities of those who report alleged misconduct. Together with RWC, we will continue to work on additional legislation in our sexual misconduct reform agenda,” she remarked in a statement earlier this week.

    Cammack remarked that, while “the entire system on Capitol Hill has been designed to create a chilling effect for victims,” the Ethics committee rule changes would help.

    Industry observers note that “Putting public disclosure of misconduct findings in writing, while protecting every victim’s identity, gives staffers a commitment they can count on. Faster investigations mean they get answers in time to matter,” Cammack stated in a statement. “This is exactly the kind of change our bipartisan task force has been pushing for.”.

    Ethics ranking member Mark DeSaulnier, D-Calif., remarked everyone in the House should have “zero tolerance” for sexual harassment.

    “We’ve worked very hard to look at ways that we could make the committee’s process fair, transparent and accountable, and I think we’ve done that,” he remarked at Thursday’s meeting.

    enSights brings AI-powered business management to solar and storage operations

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As solar and energy storage portfolios grow in both size and complexity, managing performance is just one part of the equation.
    • enSights is looking to bring those responsibilities together with the launch of its AI Studio, a newly introduced addition to its Energy Business Management (EBM) platform.
    • Recent findings suggest that the AI Studio is designed to give solar and storage owners, operators, and asset managers access to a customizable team of AI specialists that can support business and operational workflows.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As solar and energy storage portfolios grow in both size and complexity, managing performance is just one part of the equation. Owners and operators must also keep track of power purchase agreements (PPAs), warranties, service contracts, billing, compliance requirements and project-level profitability.

    enSights is looking to bring those responsibilities together with the launch of its AI Studio, a newly introduced addition to its Energy Business Management (EBM) platform. The tech giant announced the launch Nov. 10.

    Recent findings suggest that the AI Studio is designed to give solar and storage owners, operators, and asset managers access to a customizable team of AI specialists that can support business and operational workflows. Through no-code tools, consumers can create AI dashboards and reports using natural-language instructions, while still establishing their own workflows, routines, data-access permissions and approval requirements.

    The approach here reflects a broader shift toward renewable energy software, it’s moving beyond monitoring individual assets toward managing the financial and operational performance of entire portfolios.

    According to enSights, its EBM platform brings together energy management systems (EMS), production data, billing, PPA information, operations and maintenance, contractual obligations and compliance on a unified data foundation. That integration is central to the organization’s AI strategy.

    Rather than limiting AI applications to identifying equipment issues or answering generation-related questions, the platform is designed to connect energy production with the contracts and financial obligations associated with each project.

    The AI Studio includes an orchestrator that coordinates specialized AI agents focused on areas like monitoring, operations, revenue, warranties, permits, lenders, insurers, and asset management. For portfolio managers, those capabilities could help reduce the time spent reviewing disconnected systems and manually reconciling information across departments. Automated reviews of contractual obligations, revenue performance and operational alerts could also help teams identify issues earlier and direct attention to matters that still require human intervention.

    Recent findings suggest that the enSights AI Studio dashboard provides solar and energy storage operators with AI-powered tools for asset management, operational workflows, and financial oversight. Credit: enSights.

    It has been revealed that enSights emphasized that people remain in control of the AI Team. Users determine which workflows the agents handle and where approvals are required. Physical asset controls remain governed by established EMS and site-level systems.

    It has been revealed that the AI Studio also builds on an expanded financial management offering within the EBM platform. Its Financial Asset Management Module includes revenue assurance, contract, and obligation management, and profit-and-loss reporting.

    The module is intended to provide project-level financial visibility, helping companies identify and prevent revenue losses while generating reports for investors.

    The platform also includes real-time EMS, weather and tariff forecasting, along with dispatch planning intended to optimize revenue while maintaining grid safety and local compliance.

    enSights indicates its platform is deployed globally across more than 100,000 sites, representing over 5 GW of assets. The tech giant prepares to demonstrate the AI Studio and its broader EBM platform at RE+ 2026.

    As AI gains traction across the clean energy industry, the next competitive advantage could come from connecting operational intelligence with the financial and contractual decisions that determine how successfully renewable energy portfolios perform.

    Accor’s largest shareholder, Parvus Asset Management, said Thursday it will ask shareholders to remove Sébastien Bazin as chairman and CEO at the hotel group’s next annual meeting, citing Accor’s €1.6 billion (about $1.8 billion) buyout of its partners in its Ennismore joint venture and years of lagging returns.

    Parvus, which holds about 14.1% of Accor’s share capital, worth about €1.6 billion, laid out its case in a letter published Thursday. Accor’s annual meetings are typically held in May, but the next date hasn’t been set.

    Accor didn’t respond to Skift’s request for comment.

    Parvus argues Accor has long underperformed its peers. “Accor shares have returned 99% from December 2013 to November 2026, against 593% for IHG, 863% for Hilton, and 950% for Marriott,” it wrote. “In our view, this sustained gap reflects an unfocused strategy, inconsistent capital allocation, and inadequate governance oversight.”.

    Breaking: Iran resolution blocked in first war powers vote since midterms

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tim Kaine, D-Va., seen here at the Capitol on June 17, said additional war powers votes are under discussion for when Democrats control both chambers in the 120th Congress.
    • In a recent development, the Senate rejected a resolution Thursday meant to rebuke President Donald Trump over the Iran war weeks after the midterm elections demonstrated the depth of public anger about the war and its effects on the U.S.
    • Senators voted 48-51 against adopting the Iran war powers resolution that the House previously adopted in mid-September that would direct the president to withdraw U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., seen here at the Capitol on June 17, said additional war powers votes are under discussion for when Democrats control both chambers in the 120th Congress. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    In a recent development, the Senate rejected a resolution Thursday meant to rebuke President Donald Trump over the Iran war weeks after the midterm elections demonstrated the depth of public anger about the war and its effects on the U.S. economy.

    Senators voted 48-51 against adopting the Iran war powers resolution that the House previously adopted in mid-September that would direct the president to withdraw U.S. forces from the war.

    Recent findings suggest that as they have previously with similar measures, GOP Sens. Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Rand Paul of Kentucky broke with their party to support the resolution, while Democratic Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania broke with his party to oppose it. Departing GOP Sens. Thom Tillis of North Carolina and Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, who have at times voted in support of similar measures, this time voted against the resolution.

    Even if the resolution was adopted in both chambers of Congress, it would be largely symbolic since, as a concurrent resolution, it would not go to the president for his signature.

    But the vote afforded senators the opportunity to register their complaints about the war for the first time since Democrats routed Republicans in the midterm elections.

    It also comes amid a larger debate within the Democratic Party on how best to fulfill their campaign promise of ending the war as they prepare to take control of Congress next year.

    Recent findings suggest that democrats have become increasingly interested in trying to cut off funding for the war rather than continuing to hold war powers votes. But they are divided on whether to demand an immediate end to funding in the next government funding bill in December or to wait until they take power in January.

    Sources indicate that “When we have the gavels, we are contemplating other things, and we're actually contemplating things in connection with the CR discussion,” Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., told reporters Thursday in an apparent reference to the debate among Democrats.

    In a recent development, as of Nov. 13, the war has cost at least $48.3 billion, up from $47 billion last month, the nominee to be Navy comptroller, Arthur Miller, told the Senate Armed Services Committee at his confirmation hearing Thursday.

    As with previous estimates, the number Miller cited Thursday includes munitions, equipment replacement costs and operational costs but does not factor in the cost of damage to U.S. bases, which alone is likely to run in the billions.

    Industry observers note that last week, a trio of Senate Democrats unveiled legislation to prohibit funding for offensive military operations in Iran that they said they intend to introduce as an amendment to the next government funding bill, which Congress will need to pass to avoid a government shutdown after Dec. 11.

    On Thursday as the Senate voted on the war powers resolution, Sens. Tammy Duckworth, D-Ill., and Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., two of the sponsors of the proposed amendment, demanded it be included in the next funding bill.

    It has been revealed that “We’ve already tried tool after tool to get the president to rein in this conflict. Nine months in, defunding the war is the only way to force Trump to end it,” Duckworth, who vowed to vote against any continuing resolution that doesn’t include the amendment, said at a news conference.

    Industry observers note that sen. Michael Bennet, D-Colo., unveiled his own proposed amendment Thursday to bar any future and previous funding from being used to “support directly or indirectly combat activities by United States personnel in or over Iran, or in Iranian territorial waters” unless specifically authorized by Congress.

    His legislation is modeled off of language Congress passed in 1973 to cut off funding for the Nixon administration’s bombing campaign in Cambodia, Bennet’s office noted in a news release.

    In a recent development, “When we vote on short-term spending in the near future, we can fund the government and end this war. It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve,” Bennet stated in a statement.

    Meanwhile, the House is likely to vote again on a war powers resolution before year’s end.

    “Before the lame duck’s over, I hope to enforce a war powers resolution vote, and it’ll be a chance for Republicans to say whether they did or didn’t get the message on Nov. 3,” Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., mentioned Thursday in a brief interview, referring to the date of the elections.

    Recent findings suggest that as with previous resolutions, Massie’s would direct the president to remove U.S. military units from hostilities against Iran unless specifically authorized by Congress or needed to defend against an imminent attack.

    It has been revealed that the resolution was filed Nov. 10, and under the 1973 War Powers Resolution, Massie can force a vote 15 calendar days after its introduction.

    It has been revealed that john M. Donnelly and Lauren Green contributed to this report.

    Recent findings suggest that on sites that already run generators, the Mobile BESS syncs with them to cover peaks and start-up gaps, so the generators run fewer hours. Where diesel is restricted, it offers a quiet alternative.

    Recent findings suggest that where containerized storage is built to be placed once, the Mobile BESS is built to be towed and to work in any weather. It includes:.

    Industry observers note that sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., endorsed a bipartisan plan Thursday to adopt upcoming rules aimed at speeding up Senate procedures but stopped short of calling for abolishing the filibuster, laying down a marker on a key internal debate for Democrats as he positions himself to challenge Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y.

    Sources indicate that van Hollen joined Sen. Jeff Merkley, D-Ore., at a press conference Thursday to express his support for a strategy from Merkley and Sen. Steve Daines, R-Mont., to, among other changes, adopt a “talking filibuster,” requiring senators to continuously hold the floor if they seek to prevent a bill or nomination from moving forward.

    Van Hollen went further to say that while his personal view is that the filibuster itself is “anti-democratic,” changes beyond what Merkley and Daines are proposing are a matter for further discussion.

    “I’m in favor of filibuster reform,” Van Hollen mentioned. “How and when we do that is a matter for the caucus to decide.”.

    The filibuster, a Senate tactic that effectively requires a 60-vote threshold to advance most legislation, has long been the subject of calls for change or outright abolition from members of both parties.

    Other changes Merkley and Daines unveiled in October include eliminating cloture requirements for nominations and amendments, reducing post-cloture time for legislation, and introducing a fresh suspension process modeled after the House rules to allow bills with broad support to move quickly.

    Merkley actually held two separate press conferences Thursday on his filibuster proposal, one with his Montana Republican co-sponsor and then later with Van Hollen, whose bid to become majority leader he has endorsed.

    At the earlier appearance, Daines said that he thought the changes, if adopted, would “truly be a cultural change for the Senate” and lead to greater bipartisanship.

    “We believe these reforms are appropriate no matter who is in the majority, no matter what the election outcomes were,” Daines stated.

    Daines also reiterated his view that implementing any rules changes would require 67 votes from the full chamber.

    But Democrats have been debating whether to use their new majority in 2027 to change the rules on the first day of the session with 51 votes, or to eventually employ the so-called “nuclear option,” a series of procedural moves leading to a simple majority vote.

    Industry observers note that democrats used that tool in 2013 to lower the voting threshold for advancing some presidential nominations with a simple majority, rather than 60 votes. A Republican majority followed in 2017 by extending that change to include Supreme Court nominations, and again in 2019 to reduce the number of hours between a cloture and final confirmation vote.

    A spokesperson for Schumer declined to comment on Van Hollen’s endorsement of the Merkley-Daines plan.

    Schumer has noted he remains confident in his bid to remain party leader.

    Van Hollen reiterated Thursday that his “momentum is growing,” after several senators-elect have thrown their support behind the Maryland Democrat.

    “I think people recognize that if we're going to deliver on the massive things that the American voters stood up for and voted for, you can't just go back to business as usual and status quo,” Van Hollen mentioned.

    • In a recent development, russell has a museum of his own in Great Falls, Mont., but he’s also got a suite of revelatory galleries at the Montana Heritage Center in Helena, my starting point as I explored the state from west to east.

    Sources indicate that today I’ll write about Big Sky Country — Montana. I’d never been. The Mountain States aren’t the place to go for Raphaels, Rembrandts, and Renoirs, but there are treasures to be found. What ought to be there? I very easily found my answer: Montana’s own Charles M. Russell, the perceptive, precise artist famous for his cowboy pictures but proudest of his scenes of Montana’s Chippewa, Blood Indian, and Lakota Natives. At 16, Russell (1864–1926) left school in Missouri to work on a sheep ranch in Montana. He lived under those spacious skies for the rest of his life, making thousands of works of art. A contemporary of Frederic Remington, he’s less known but just as good if not better.

    In a recent development, russell has a museum of his own in Great Falls, Mont., but he’s also got a suite of revelatory galleries at the Montana Heritage Center in Helena, my starting point as I explored the state from west to east. The Heritage Center, whose galleries are filled with art and artifacts from Montana’s Historical Society, opened late last year after a $160 million expansion and renovation. It’s wonderful. The Russell section is more or less chronological and a mix of art, hagiography, and atmosphere. I loved it. The entire newly introduced complex is great. It’s got a Russell section as well as multiple galleries on Montana’s history.

    Brian T. Allen is National Review’s art critic.

    On “A Swing Through Montana’s Art Treasures”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    OMCO Solar now offers a version of its OMCO Star Tracker Control System powered entirely by solar energy, allowing tracker controls to operate without AC power at the site.

    Industry observers note that the system, first introduced last year, is designed for OMCO Origin Factory-Direct Trackers. Its tracker controllers, array controllers and sensor bridges use all-weather battery packs charged by solar modules.

    According to OMCO, the technology eliminates the need for AC power to tracker control components and an uninterruptible power supply. It also allows tracker controls to operate and protects modules against wind, snow and hail before AC power is available.

    Recent findings suggest that “Our industry has solved so many problems as we have grown – we’re now the leading source for upcoming electric energy capacity in the US. This addition to the OMCO Star product line solves one more – how to protect modules if there’s no AC power to the site even for a short time. We’re excited to offer this solution to our existing customers and to new partners,” said Matt Kesler, vice president of solar technology at OMCO Solar, in a statement.

    The OMCO Star system uses LoRa, or long-range, wireless technology with a communication range greater than 1 mile. According to OMCO, this reduces the number of network controllers required and allows direct communication with every tracker without relying on a mesh network.

    The manufacturer indicates LoRa is 100 times less susceptible to electromagnetic noise than Zigbee and better able to connect to distant trackers despite obstacles.

    It has been revealed that OMCO claims its all-weather battery packs allow the solar-powered controls to operate reliably in cold climates. The system includes field-replaceable batteries, a phone app that eliminates the need for buttons on controllers and a remote monitoring and control portal.

    Sources indicate that the portal allows operators to move trackers for activities such as mowing, snow plowing and module cleaning. The system is developed, manufactured and supported by OMCO Solar in the United States.

    “We are excited about bringing this innovation to the Utility Scale and DG tracker markets. Over the past few years, OMCO has expanded its capabilities beyond just being a US steel manufacturer to now being a true technology leader in our space. We look forward to supporting our customers/partners with the OMCO Star Tracker Control System, improving reliability, and reducing the labor and materials needed to build their projects,” said Eric Goodwin, vice president of business development at OMCO Solar.

    OMCO Solar will display the all-DC tracker control system at RE+ in Las Vegas, November 17–19, in the North Hall, booth N516.
